definition_zh: 有益健康的；有利身心的；健康的
definition_en: good for your health, or likely to make you healthy
core_image: 一盘新鲜蔬果与一杯清水，摆在晨光里的餐桌上
scene: 营养课上，老师指着餐盘里的蔬菜和水果，告诉学生哪些食物真正对身体有益。In the nutrition class, the teacher pointed at the vegetables and fruit on the tray and told the students that the leafy vegetables are healthful for people of every age.
sceneCN: 这里 healthful 是「有益健康的」（第 1 个义项：能促进健康的事物）；句意：营养课上，老师指着餐盘里的蔬菜和水果，告诉学生这些绿叶蔬菜对各年龄段的人都有益健康。

pos.zh: 健康的；身体状态良好的（多见于美式用法）

derivatives.zh: 由 healthful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「有益健康地」
由 healthful 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「有益健康的性质」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「有害健康的」
由 healthy 加 -ly 构成，义为「健康地」

senses.title: Good for health
senses.definition: likely to keep a person healthy or to make health better
senses.definitionCN: 能够让人保持健康或使身体状态变好的
senses.example: A healthful breakfast gives children the energy they need.
senses.exampleCN: 一顿有益健康的早餐能给孩子提供所需的能量。
senses.why: The noun health names the healthy state, and the suffix -ful means full of, so healthful describes anything that fills a person with health.
senses.whyCN: 名词 health 指健康的状态，后缀 -ful 表示「充满……的」，所以 healthful 描述的是能把健康带给人的事物。

senses.title: Wholesome in a wider sense
senses.definition: morally sound and likely to do good, used of air, climate, habits, or activities
senses.definitionCN: 在道德或身心上都有益的，常用于气候、环境、习惯或活动
senses.example: The mountain air is clean and healthful.
senses.exampleCN: 山里的空气洁净而有益健康。
senses.why: Health is both physical and mental, so the adjective widens from food and medicine to any condition that nourishes body and mind.
senses.whyCN: 健康既包括身体也涉及精神，于是这个形容词从食物、药物扩大到了任何滋养身心的条件。

senses.title: Being in good health
senses.definition: having good health, a use common in American English for people and animals
senses.definitionCN: 身体状态良好，这种用法在美式英语中常用于人和动物
senses.example: She looked healthful after a summer on the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 在农场待了一个夏天之后，她看上去很健康。
senses.why: The distinction between the cause of health and the possession of health is thin in speech, so healthful came to describe the person as well as the food.
senses.whyCN: 在口语里，「带来健康的因素」与「拥有健康」的界限很细微，于是 healthful 也从形容食物扩展到形容人本身。

senses.title: Sound in mind and habit
senses.definition: serving a sensible and beneficial purpose, as of reading, exercise, or pastime
senses.definitionCN: 指读书、锻炼或消遣等有正当且有益的作用
senses.example: Jogging is a healthful pastime for busy office workers.
senses.exampleCN: 慢跑对忙碌的上班族来说是一项有益健康的消遣。
senses.why: What preserves the body is easily extended to what preserves the character, giving a moral shade to an originally medical word.
senses.whyCN: 保全身体的事物很容易延伸到保全品性的事物，于是一个原本属于医学的词带上了道德的意味。

senses.title: A healthful amount or balance
senses.definition: of a safe, balanced quantity in diet, exercise, or rest
senses.definitionCN: 指饮食、运动或休息方面安全而平衡的量
senses.example: Nutritionists talk about healthful portions rather than strict limits.
senses.exampleCN: 营养学家讨论的是有益健康的分量，而不是严格的限制。
senses.why: When the word is applied to quantity, it names the amount that supports health instead of harming it, a natural step from the goodness of the whole to the rightness of the dose.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词用在数量上时，它指的是支持健康而非损害健康的量，这是从整体的「有益」自然过渡到剂量的「合适」。

senses.title: Healthful in official advice
senses.definition: labeling a food, home, or programme that meets an approved standard of benefit
senses.definitionCN: 为食品、住宅或项目标注符合公认有益标准
senses.example: The council printed a list of healthful meals for school canteens.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会为学校食堂印发了一份健康膳食清单。
senses.why: Public bodies often choose healthful over healthy to avoid the ambiguity of a word that can also mean merely well, and the term settles into official wording.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构常选用 healthful 而非 healthy，以避开后者也能表示「身体尚可」的歧义，这个词于是固定进官方措辞。

senses.title: A healthful state of a place
senses.definition: used of a place, climate, or system that supports lasting well being
senses.definitionCN: 指地方、气候或系统能长期支持身心良好
senses.example: Writers of that era praised the healthful climate of the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时代的作家称赞沿海的气候有利于健康。
senses.why: Places were once judged by whether they kept residents well, so healthful became a word for describing climate and landscape.
senses.whyCN: 过去人们会以一处地方能否让居民保持健康来衡量它，于是 healthful 成了描述气候与风景的词。

senses.title: Healthful contrasted with healthy
senses.titleCN: 与 healthy 的用法区别
senses.definition: the choice of healthful emphasizes the power to cause health rather than the condition of having it
senses.definitionCN: 选用 healthful 强调的是产生健康的作用，而不是拥有健康的状态
senses.example: Careful editors prefer a healthful meal to a healthy one.
senses.exampleCN: 严谨的编辑更愿意说一顿有益健康的饭，而不是「一顿健康的饭」。
senses.why: Grammar guides long drew the line between the cause and the possessor of health, and the word keeps that contrast for careful writers.
senses.whyCN: 语法书长期把「带来健康的因素」和「拥有健康的人」区分开来，这个词在严谨的作者笔下就保留了这一对照。

intro.en: Healthful is built on the noun health plus the suffix -ful, first recorded in English in the late sixteenth century.
intro.cn: healthful 由名词 health 加后缀 -ful 构成，英语中最早见于十六世纪后期。

items.en: Hal means whole or sound, and the noun hal develops into modern health.
items.cn: 古英语形容词 hal 意为完整的、健全的，同源名词后来演变为现代英语的 health。

items.en: The related adjective hal names the healthy state of a body.
items.cn: 古英语名词 hæl 表示身体健全康健的状态，是 health 的直接前身。

items.en: Middle English helthe fixes the noun sense of the healthy condition.
items.cn: 中古英语 helthe 把「健康状态」这一名词义固定下来。

items.en: The suffix -ful, meaning full of, is added to health to form the adjective.
items.cn: 表示「充满……的」后缀 -ful 加在 health 上，构成这个形容词。

items.en: Healthful is used of climates, air, and habits that preserve good health.
items.cn: healthful 用于描述能保持健康的空气、气候与生活习惯。

items.en: Usage guides separate healthful as the cause of health from healthy as the state.
items.cn: 现代用法指南把 healthful 看作健康的原因，把 healthy 看作健康的状态。

note.en: Healthful belongs to the health family and is often contrasted with healthy and wholesome.
note.cn: healthful 属于「健康」词族，常与 healthy、wholesome 对照使用。

entries.definitionCN: 身体或精神健全的状态

entries.definition: in good health, or good for health
entries.definitionCN: 健康的；也有时指有益健康的

entries.definition: the quality of being good for health

entries.definition: good for health, both physically and morally
entries.definitionCN: 有益健康的，兼指身心

entries.definition: producing a good effect

entries.definition: rich in the substances that the body needs
entries.definitionCN: 营养丰富的

entries.definition: pleasant and good for the health of a place
entries.definitionCN: 宜人的；有利于健康的

normalIntro.en: Healthful is health plus the suffix -ful, so it names anything full of health-giving power.
normalIntro.cn: healthful 就是 health 加上后缀 -ful，指的是充满「带来健康之力」的事物。

normal.en: Health is the noun and -ful means full of, so healthful means full of health.
normal.cn: health 是名词，-ful 表示充满，所以 healthful 意为「充满健康的」。

normal.en: A healthful diet is what a doctor would recommend.
normal.cn: healthful diet 指医生会推荐的饮食。

normal.en: Healthful describes the food or climate, while healthy describes the person.
normal.cn: healthful 形容食物或气候有益健康，healthy 则形容人身体好。

normal.en: The adverb healthfully and the noun healthfulness share the same base.
normal.cn: 副词 healthfully 与名词 healthfulness 共用同一个词基。

normal.en: Wholesome is the closer cousin in everyday talk.
normal.cn: 在日常口语里，wholesome 是更亲近的同义说法。

abstract.en: Picture a plate of greens glowing as if it were charging a body with energy.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘青菜在发光，仿佛正给身体充电。

abstract.en: Imagine sea air filling the lungs on a clear winter walk.
abstract.cn: 想象冬日的海边散步，清爽的空气灌满肺里。

abstract.en: Think of a morning jogger whose face is fresh every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一位晨跑者，脸色每天都红润有神。

examples.en: The school serves healthful meals with plenty of vegetables.
examples.cn: 这所学校提供蔬菜充足的有益健康的饭菜。

examples.en: Doctors say a healthful lifestyle protects the heart.
examples.cn: 医生说健康的生活方式能保护心脏。

examples.en: The dry mountain climate was once thought healthful.
examples.cn: 干燥的山地气候过去被认为有益健康。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑尔歇福」——听着像「歇一歇就有福」，身体能歇好、有福气，就是有益健康的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hæl（完整的、健全的）→ 同源名词 hæl（健康）→ 中古英语 helthe → 现代英语 health，加后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成 healthful，核心义「充满健康之力」。

sensesIntro.en: Healthful starts as the adjective of what gives health, then widens to wholesome conditions and even to persons, ending as a usage contrast with healthy.
sensesIntro.cn: healthful 先指「带来健康的事物」，再扩展到有益身心的情况乃至人本身，最后成为与 healthy 对照的用法问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate of greens and a glass of water on a sunlit table.
core.cn: 核心意象：晨光餐桌上的一盘青菜与一杯清水。

branches.en: What is good for health is the central sense.
branches.cn: 对健康有益是核心义项。

branches.en: The wholesome sense widens the word to air, habits, and climate.
branches.cn: 有益身心这一义项把词扩展到空气、习惯和气候。

branches.en: The person who is well is the American use.
branches.cn: 身体健康的人是美式用法的义项。

branches.en: Soundness of purpose and a safe amount both preserve health.
branches.cn: 健全的用意与合适的量都能维护健康。

branches.en: Official wording, places, and the healthy contrast build the modern usage.
branches.cn: 官方措辞、地点与同 healthy 的对照构成了现代用法。

intro.en: Healthful is a suffix-built word inside the health family, with -ful, -ly, -ness, and un- all productive around it.
intro.cn: healthful 是「健康」词族中用后缀构成的词，围绕它还有 -ful、-ly、-ness、un- 等能产词缀。

latinIntro.en: The base comes from Old English hal, so the family has no Latin root and the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古英语 hal，这个词族没有拉丁词根，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

definition_zh: 传闻；道听途说；传闻证据
definition_en: information heard from someone else without proof that it is true
core_image: 一句话从一张嘴传到另一只耳朵，中间没有纸笔，也没有见证人
scene: 办公室里没人见过那份文件，大家只是互相耳语，说公司下个月要搬家。No one in the office has seen the file, yet everyone is busy passing on hearsay about the company moving next month.
sceneCN: 这里 hearsay 是「传闻」（第 1 个义项：从别人口中听来、未经证实的消息）；句意：办公室里没人见过那份文件，可大家都在忙着传递公司下月搬迁的传闻。

pos.zh: 传闻的（多用于法律，如传闻证据）

collocations.zh: 把某事当作传闻而不予理会

derivatives.zh: 复合词的第一部分，义为「听见」
复合词的第二部分，义为「说出」
由 hear 加 -ing 构成，义为「听证会；倾听」
复合形容词，义为「基于传闻的」

senses.title: News heard from others
senses.definition: information that a person has heard from others rather than seen or checked
senses.definitionCN: 从旁人那里听来、而非亲眼所见或亲自核实的消息
senses.example: It is only hearsay that the company will close.
senses.exampleCN: 公司要倒闭的说法只是传闻而已。
senses.why: The word is hear plus say, so it names exactly the chain of a message passing from a mouth to an ear without a witness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 hear 和 say 两部分组成，正好指向消息从一张嘴传到另一只耳朵、却没有见证人的那条链。

senses.title: Unverified and second-hand
senses.definition: news that is passed along without evidence and may well be false
senses.definitionCN: 辗转相传、缺乏证据、很可能并不属实的消息
senses.example: Do not repeat this kind of talk as if it were fact.
senses.exampleCN: 不要把这种说法当成事实来传。
senses.why: Because the listener never watched the event, the word carries a built in doubt and turns into a label for unreliable talk.
senses.whyCN: 因为听者从未亲眼见过那件事，词义自带了怀疑，于是变成对不可靠说法的标签。

senses.title: Evidence not based on direct observation
senses.definition: a statement in court that repeats what someone else said outside the court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上复述他人在庭外所说内容的口头证据
senses.example: The judge refused to admit hearsay as proof.
senses.exampleCN: 法官拒绝把传闻作为证据采纳。
senses.why: Courts need the person who saw or heard the event, so second-hand speech becomes a named category of excluded evidence.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要亲眼所见或亲耳所闻的人作证，于是二手说法成了一个被排除的证据类别。

senses.title: Gossip and idle rumour
senses.definition: small talk that spreads from person to person, often about neighbours or colleagues
senses.definitionCN: 在人与人之间传播的闲话，常涉及邻里或同事
senses.example: Much of the village hearsay was harmless but cruel.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的许多流言并无恶意，却很伤人。
senses.why: The same mouth to ear chain that carries news also carries gossip, so the word drifts into the everyday language of rumours.
senses.whyCN: 传播消息的那条「口耳相传」链条同样传播闲话，于是这个词滑进了日常的谣言语境。

senses.title: Opinion that others reported
senses.definition: a view or report that the speaker repeats but did not form or test
senses.definitionCN: 说话人只是转述、既未自己形成也未验证的意见或报告
senses.example: His complaint was hearsay from a cousin in the trade.
senses.exampleCN: 他的抱怨只是从一位做这行的表亲那里听来的。
senses.why: A claim can be borrowed without its grounds, and hearsay labels any position inherited by repetition rather than by thinking.
senses.whyCN: 一个说法可以被借来却带不来依据，hearsay 就用来标注一切靠重复而非靠思考继承来的立场。

senses.title: Folk knowledge and old stories
senses.definition: traditional sayings or stories repeated over generations without a clear source
senses.definitionCN: 世代相传、却没有清楚来源的传统说法或故事
senses.example: The recipe survives only as hearsay in two families.
senses.exampleCN: 这个做法只靠口耳相传，仅存于两个家庭之中。
senses.why: Long before print and recording, knowledge lived in repetition, so hearsay can describe the ordinary channel of tradition as well as the risk of error.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷和录音出现之前，知识靠重复流传，所以 hearsay 既能指传统的日常渠道，也能指出错的风险。

senses.title: A label of distrust
senses.definition: a word used to reject a report as belonging to no reliable source
senses.definitionCN: 用来否认一份报告来自可靠来源的贬称
senses.example: He waved the warning away as mere hearsay.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那则警告当作纯属传言，置之一旁。
senses.why: Once hearsay is excluded from proof, the same noun becomes an efficient way to dismiss a claim without arguing against it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 hearsay 被排除在证据之外，这个名词就成了不必反驳就能打发一个说法的便捷方式。

senses.title: The old noun for reputation
senses.definition: the opinion people hold of someone, an older and now rare sense
senses.definitionCN: 人们对某人的看法，这是较古老而如今少见的义项
senses.example: In older writing, a quiet neighbour could win praise through the talk of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 在更早的写作里，一位安静的邻居可以靠镇上的风评赢得称许。
senses.why: What people say about a person is both reputation and rumour, so the early noun covered the good name as well as the mere talk.
senses.whyCN: 人们口中的议论既可以是名誉，也可以是流言，所以早期的名词既包括「好名声」也包括「空口议论」。

intro.en: Hearsay is an English compound of hear and say, recorded from the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: hearsay 是英语自造的复合词，由 hear 与 say 合成，文献记载可追溯到十六世纪。

items.en: Heran means to hear, and secgan means to say or tell.
items.cn: 古英语 古英语动词 heran 意为听见，动词 secgan 意为说、讲述。

items.en: The noun hering covers what is heard and reported.
items.cn: 中古英语名词 hering 指所听到、被转述的内容。

items.en: Hearsay appears in law reports as speech based on what another person said.
items.cn: hearsay 在十六世纪的法律文书中出现，指基于他人转述的说法。

items.en: Courts develop the hearsay rule and treat second-hand statements with suspicion.
items.cn: 法院逐渐形成传闻证据规则，对二手陈述持怀疑态度。

items.en: Hearsay widens into everyday talk for unproven gossip and second-hand news.
items.cn: hearsay 扩展到日常口语，指未经证实的流言与二手消息。

note.en: Hearsay is a mouth to ear word, close in form to hear and say and close in meaning to rumour and gossip.
note.cn: hearsay 是一个「口耳相传」的词，形式上与 hear、say 相近，意义上与 rumour、gossip 相邻。

entries.definition: to notice a sound with the ears
entries.definitionCN: 用耳朵听到声音

entries.definition: to speak words
entries.definitionCN: 说出话语

entries.definition: the ability to hear, or an official session where facts are heard
entries.definitionCN: 听觉；听证会

entries.definition: a story that spreads without proof and is often false
entries.definitionCN: 无根据流传、常为不实的说法

entries.definition: talk about other people and their private lives
entries.definitionCN: 议论他人私事的闲话

entries.definition: guessing about something without firm facts
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏事实依据的猜测

normalIntro.en: Hearsay is what you hear someone say and then pass on, so the two verbs of the chain sit inside this compound.
normalIntro.cn: hearsay 就是你「听见」别人「说」、再转述出去的东西，这条链上的两个动词就嵌在这个复合词里。

normal.en: Hear plus say describes the whole journey of a rumour by itself.
normal.cn: hear 加 say，本身就描述了流言从听到说的整段旅程。

normal.en: Mere hearsay means a claim with no proof behind it.
normal.cn: mere hearsay 指毫无凭据的说法。

normal.en: In law, the hearsay rule keeps second-hand statements out of court.
normal.cn: 在法律上，关于二手证据的规则把这类陈述挡在法庭之外。

normal.en: If you can only say who told you, not what you saw, you have a case of second-hand talk.
normal.cn: 如果你只能说出是谁告诉你的，却说不出自己看见了什么，那就属于二手说法。

normal.en: Rumour is the near synonym, and both share the same mouth to ear picture.
normal.cn: rumour 是近义词，两者共享同一个「口耳相传」的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence hopping from one ear to the next like a whisper carried in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话像随风而走的悄悄话，从一只耳朵跳到另一只耳朵。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand whisper passing along a line of children in a playground.
abstract.cn: 想象操场上孩子们排成一列，悄悄话从一个人传到下一个人。

abstract.en: Picture a judge holding up a witness statement with a red cross through it.
abstract.cn: 想象法官举起一份被红色叉号划掉的证人陈述。

examples.en: Much of what she told me was pure gossip passed on at the market.
examples.cn: 她告诉我的大多是集市上随口传来的闲话。

examples.en: The court ruled that the statement was hearsay and excluded it.
examples.cn: 法院裁定该陈述属于传闻证据，予以排除。

examples.en: A good reporter never prints a story based on hearsay alone.
examples.cn: 优秀的记者绝不会仅凭传闻就刊发报道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「听说」——hear 是听，say 是说，听别人说来的话就是传闻；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 heran（听见）+ secgan（说）→ 中古英语 hering（所听之言）→ 十六世纪复合词 hearsay（听来的说法）→ 现代英语延伸出法律义「传闻证据」。

sensesIntro.en: Hearsay begins as news heard from someone else, develops into unproven talk and legal evidence, and finally becomes a label of distrust.
sensesIntro.cn: hearsay 先指从别人那里听来的消息，再发展为未经证实的说法与法律证据，最后变成一种表示不可信的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence passing from one mouth to another ear with no witness.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话从一张嘴传到另一只耳朵，没有见证人。

branches.en: News heard from others is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 从别人处听来的消息是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Unproven talk, gossip, and reported opinion share the missing witness.
branches.cn: 未经证实的说法、流言与转述的看法都缺少见证人。

branches.en: The legal sense turns the word into a category of evidence.
branches.cn: 法律义项把该词变成了一个证据类别。

branches.en: Folk knowledge shows the word as an old channel of tradition.
branches.cn: 民间说法显示该词也曾是传统的传播渠道。

branches.en: The label of distrust and the old sense of reputation close the circle.
branches.cn: 表示不可信的标签与旧的名声义项回到了「议论」的原点。

intro.en: Hearsay is built from two native English verbs, without a Latin or French stem.
intro.cn: hearsay 由两个本土英语动词合成，没有拉丁或法语词干。

latinIntro.en: The elements come from Old English heran and secgan, so there is no Latin root and the list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分来自古英语 heran 与 secgan，没有拉丁词根，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Say is the second element.

items.example: The noun hearing covers the listening side.
items.exampleCN: 名词 hearing 涵盖「听」的一面。

items.example: The noun saying keeps the spoken side.
items.exampleCN: 名词 saying 保留「说」的一面。

items.meaning: a formula marking a common saying
items.meaningCN: 标明「常言道」的固定说法
items.example: This formula marks talk that is merely repeated.
items.exampleCN: 这个句式用来标明只是被重复的传言。

items.meaning: news spread by speaking rather than writing
items.meaningCN: 靠口耳相传而非书面传播的消息
items.example: Word of mouth is the everyday cousin of hearsay.

definition_en: to make someone feel more cheerful, confident, or determined
core_image: 一只手轻轻按在低落之人的肩上，那人的背慢慢挺直
scene: 球队在上半场落后两个球，教练走进更衣室，拍拍队员的肩膀，让大家重新振作起来。Two goals down at half time, the coach went into the changing room to hearten the players before the second half.
sceneCN: 这里 hearten 是「使振奋、使鼓舞」（第 2 个义项：给低落的人注入勇气与信心）；句意：半场落后两球时，教练走进更衣室，在第二半场前给队员们打气。

collocations.zh: 因这个消息而受到鼓舞

derivatives.zh: 由 hearten 加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「令人振奋的」
过去分词用作形容词，义为「受到鼓舞的」
加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「使泄气、使沮丧」
同根形容词，义为「真诚的；丰盛的」

senses.title: To give strength to the heart
senses.titleCN: 使有了心气；使重拾力量
senses.definition: to restore strength of spirit to someone who feels low or tired
senses.definitionCN: 给情绪低落或疲惫的人重新注入精神力量
senses.example: A kindly word heartened the tired helper.
senses.exampleCN: 一句亲切的话让疲惫的帮手重新有了力气。
senses.why: The word is heart plus the verb ending -en, so hearten literally means to put heart into a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 heart 加上动词词尾 -en 构成，所以 hearten 字面意思就是「把心放进一个人身上」。

senses.title: To lift a low mood
senses.definition: to make someone feel more hopeful, confident, or cheerful
senses.definitionCN: 使人更有希望、更有信心或更愉快
senses.example: The coach tried to hearten the players before the final.
senses.exampleCN: 教练想在决赛前给队员们打气。
senses.why: A heart that is low is a heart that is short of courage, and filling it again is the everyday sense of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 情绪低落的心就是缺了勇气的心，重新把它填满，就是这个词的日常意义。

senses.title: To encourage to keep going
senses.definition: to give someone the courage to face a task or a danger
senses.definitionCN: 给某人勇气去面对任务或危险
senses.example: Her calm voice heartened the climbers.
senses.exampleCN: 她从容的声音给了登山者勇气。
senses.why: Courage was long thought to sit in the heart, so to hearten a person is to arm that inner seat of courage.
senses.whyCN: 勇气自古被看作住在心里，所以 hearten 一个人，就是为这个勇气的内座增添武装。

senses.title: News that raises hopes
senses.definition: to be encouraged by good news, a sign, or a result
senses.definitionCN: 因好消息、迹象或结果而受到激励
senses.example: Investors were heartened by the rising figures.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者因不断上升的数据而受到鼓舞。
senses.why: When a single fact lifts a group, the verb can take the news as its cause and the group as its object in the passive.
senses.whyCN: 当一个事实让一群人精神一振时，这个动词可以在被动式中以消息为原因、以人群为对象。

senses.title: To cheer a crowd
senses.definition: to strengthen the spirit of a group such as an audience or a team
senses.definitionCN: 增强观众、队伍等群体的精神士气
senses.example: The drums heartened the marchers through the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 鼓声在雨中一路给游行者打气。
senses.why: Founded on heart, the verb suits groups as well as single persons, so music and speeches can hearten a whole crowd.
senses.whyCN: 以 heart 为词基，这个动词既适用于单个的人，也适用于群体，所以音乐和演讲都能给一整群人带来鼓舞。

senses.title: To feel cheered oneself
senses.definition: to become brave or cheerful, a use of the verb found in older writing
senses.definitionCN: 使自己变得勇敢或愉快，这是旧文献里出现的自反用法
senses.example: He heartened himself with a brisk walk.
senses.exampleCN: 他快步走了一趟，让自己振作起来。
senses.why: Older English often let a verb stand alone, so the subject could hearten himself as well as another person.
senses.whyCN: 早期英语常让某个动词单独使用，所以主语既可以让别人振作，也可以让自己振作。

senses.title: Opposite of disheartening
senses.definition: the positive partner of dishearten, meaning to raise the spirits that worry has lowered
senses.definitionCN: 与 dishearten 相对的积极词，指把忧虑压低的心气重新提起来
senses.example: The small progress heartened the volunteers, not disheartened them.
senses.exampleCN: 这点小进展让志愿者们振奋，而不是灰心。
senses.why: The negation dis- turns the verb into its opposite, and the plain form keeps the job of undoing discouragement.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 dis- 把这个动词变成反义，原形则承担起消除泄气的任务。

senses.title: A heartening sign
senses.definition: used to describe a result or sign that gives people fresh confidence
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述给人新信心的结果或迹象
senses.example: It is heartening to see the numbers rise.
senses.exampleCN: 看到数字上升，实在令人振奋。
senses.why: From the verb grows the adjective heartening, which names and praises whatever produces the lift.
senses.whyCN: 由这个动词派生出形容词 heartening，用来指称并称赞那些带来提振的事物。

intro.en: Hearten is an English word made from the native noun heart with the verb ending -en.
intro.cn: hearten 是英语本土构词，由名词 heart 加上动词词尾 -en 组成。

items.en: Heorte means the heart and also the seat of feeling and courage.
items.cn: 古英语 heorte 指心脏，也指情感与勇气的所在。

items.en: The spelling settles towards heart, and this word keeps both the bodily and the mental sense.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 heart，这个词同时保留身体与精神两层含义。

items.en: The verb ending -en shapes hearten from the noun, following the pattern of strengthen.
items.cn: 仿照 strengthen 的构造方式，动词词尾 -en 加在名词 heart 上构成了 hearten。

items.en: The opposite dishearten appears alongside, and the pair is used of moods and troops.
items.cn: 反义词 dishearten 紧接着出现，这对词用于描述情绪与队伍。

items.en: Hearten lives mostly in written and polite speech, while heartening survives in news.
items.cn: hearten 主要用于书面或较正式的言语，而 heartening 在新闻报道中留存。

note.en: Hearten belongs to the heart family, with derived forms, and sits close to encourage and reassure.
note.cn: hearten 属于「心」词族，有规范的派生形式，意义上与 encourage、reassure 相邻。

definition_zh: 冷酷无情的；没心没肺的；残忍的；没有感情色彩的
definition_en: showing no concern or kindness for other people or other living things
core_image: 胸口的位置空空的，只剩一副衣架挂着外衣
scene: 大雨里一只小狗被扔在路边，路过的人谁也不肯停车。A heartless driver left the small dog alone in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 heartless 是「冷酷无情的」（第 1 个义项：对别人毫无恻隐之心）；句意：一个冷酷的司机把这只小狗独自丢在雨里。

pos.zh: 没心没肺的；无忧无虑的（口语）
缺乏人情味的；无感情色彩的

collocations.zh: 既冷酷又自私（并列说法）

derivatives.zh: 由 heartless 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「冷酷地；无情地」
由 heartless 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「冷酷无情」

senses.title: Showing no kindness or concern
senses.definition: showing no concern for the suffering of others and no wish to help
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的痛苦毫不在乎，也不愿意出手相助
senses.example: It was heartless of them to refuse the child food.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拒绝给那孩子食物，真是冷酷无情。
senses.why: The suffix -less means without, so heartless literally means without a heart, and the heart has long stood for feeling.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -less 表示「没有」，所以 heartless 字面就是「没有心」，而心一直代表感情与同情，没有心自然就是不施善意。

senses.title: Cruel and pitiless in an act
senses.definition: the description of an action or plan that fully ignores what others will suffer
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容完全不顾他人将承受何种痛苦的行为或计划
senses.example: The heartless removal of the tenants left families on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 把房客赶走这件事残忍至极，几家人流落街头。
senses.why: When the missing heart is turned outward into an action, the lack of concern becomes visible cruelty.
senses.whyCN: 当「缺了的那颗心」落到一个具体动作上，缺失的关怀就变成了看得见的残忍。

senses.title: Carefree, without serious thought
senses.titleCN: 没心没肺的；无忧无虑的
senses.definition: so light-minded that one does not take things seriously; in modern usage very rare with this meaning
senses.definitionCN: 心思很轻，凡事不当真；现代英语中这个意思已非常少见
senses.example: The heartless youth went on laughing while others quarrelled.
senses.exampleCN: 这个没心没肺的年轻人继续笑着，别人却吵作一团。
senses.why: Older English used heartless for lacking courage or feeling in a light sense, and the same empty-heart image can show no heaviness of mind when it is used without cruelty.
senses.whyCN: 旧英语里的 heartless 曾带有「没胆量、没心思」的轻淡意味；同一幅空心画面在不用来指责残忍时，就表示心里不装事、毫无负担。

senses.title: Lacking human warmth or sentiment
senses.definition: describing systems, places, or styles that give out no warmth or human feeling
senses.definitionCN: 形容制度、场所或风格不带温度、没有人情味
senses.example: They call the city a heartless machine of steel and glass.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这城市称作一台由钢铁和玻璃构成的、毫无人情味的机器。
senses.why: When the missing heart spreads from people to things, buildings and rules are judged by the same warmth standard.
senses.whyCN: 当「空心」从人扩展到事物，建筑和规则也会被用同一把「有没有温度」的尺子来评判。

intro.en: Heartless is formed inside English from heart and the native suffix -less, without any borrowing from Latin or French.
intro.cn: heartless 是在英语内部由 heart 加本族语后缀 -less 构成的，并未向拉丁语或法语借用。

items.en: Heorte means the bodily organ and the seat of feeling, mind, and courage.
items.cn: 古英语 heorte 既指身体的器官，也指感情、心思与勇气的所在。

items.en: The suffix -leas means without and builds many personal adjectives.
items.cn: 后缀 -leas 意为「没有」，能构成许多描述人的形容词。

items.era: OLD ENGLISH TO MIDDLE ENGLISH, 12TH–13TH C.
items.en: Heartless is formed, and early records use it for lacking courage or lacking feeling.
items.cn: heartless 在这一时期构成，早期文献用它表示「缺乏胆量」或「没有感情」。

items.en: The word is used for actions and people that show no pity, which becomes the main sense.
items.cn: 这个词开始用于形容毫无怜悯的行为与人，这成为它的主要义项。

items.en: The light sense of being carefree survives only rarely, while the cruel sense dominates modern usage.
items.cn: 「没心没肺」这一轻淡义项如今已很少见，现代用法以「冷酷残忍」为主。

note.en: Heartless sits in the -less family built on heart, and stands near the whole group of words that judge what a person lacks.
note.cn: heartless 属于以 heart 为中心、由 -less 构成的一族词，并和整组表示「某人缺乏什么」的词相邻。

entries.definition: the organ, or the seat of feeling and courage
