entries.definition: warm, cheerful, and generous
entries.definitionCN: 热情的；诚挚的（与 heartless 同以 heart 为基）

entries.definition: a feeling of very deep sadness
entries.definitionCN: 心碎；极度悲伤

entries.definition: causing pain without caring
entries.definitionCN: 残忍的；使人受苦而毫不在意

entries.definition: made insensitive to suffering by long habit
entries.definitionCN: 麻木不仁的（因习惯而不再对痛苦有反应；heartless 更强调天生无情）

entries.definition: showing no mercy, often in a definite purpose
entries.definitionCN: 毫不留情的；残酷的

normalIntro.en: Heartless is heart plus -less, a very common English way of saying something is missing.
normalIntro.cn: heartless 就是 heart 加 -less，这是英语里非常常用的「缺少某物」构词法。

normal.en: The suffix -less means without, so heartless is without heart.
normal.cn: 后缀 -less 表示「没有」，因此 heartless 就是「没有心」。

normal.en: Compare hopeless, homeless, and harmless, which also use -less.
normal.cn: 对比 hopeless、homeless、harmless，它们同样使用 -less。

normal.en: Heartlessness is the noun and heartlessly is the adverb built from the same stem.
normal.cn: heartlessness 是名词，heartlessly 是副词，都出自同一个词干。

normal.en: The heart has long meant warm feeling, so the word is about feeling rather than physical life.
normal.cn: 心一直象征温情，所以这个词说的是感情层面的东西，而不是生理上的生命。

normal.en: In the old light sense the word described someone carefree, but now it almost always criticises cruelty.
normal.cn: 旧的轻淡用法形容「没心没肺、不装事」的人，而今天它几乎总是在指责残忍。

abstract.en: Picture a coat on a hanger with nothing inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外衣挂在衣架上，里面空空如也。

abstract.en: Picture a cold hand pushing a plate away from a hungry child.
abstract.cn: 想象一只冷冰冰的手把一盘饭从饥饿的孩子面前推开。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd laughing and talking, each person looking past the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人笑着聊天，每个人的目光都越过别人。

examples.en: It was heartless to leave the animals without food.
examples.cn: 不给这些动物喂食，实在太冷酷了。

examples.en: She called the plan heartless and demanded a fair review.
examples.cn: 她称这个计划不近人情，要求重新公平审议。

examples.en: His heartless reply ended the conversation at once.
examples.cn: 他那冷酷的回答一下子让对话结束了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「哈特勒斯」——名字叫「哈特」的勒斯，哈哈一笑就把人推开，心肠冷；只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 heorte（心脏；感情、心思与勇气）+ 后缀 -leas（没有）→ 中古英语 heartless，核心义「心里没有感情」。

sensesIntro.en: Heartless starts from not caring about others, then turns into visible cruelty, then recalls a light carefree sense, and finally extends to places and systems without warmth.
sensesIntro.cn: heartless 从「不顾他人」出发，进而指看得见的残忍，又保留一个「没心没肺」的轻淡义项，最后扩展到毫无温度的地方与制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest with nothing inside, holding no feeling for others.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口空无一物，对他人没有任何感情。

branches.en: No concern for others is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 对他人毫不在乎是日常核心义项。

branches.en: Cruel acts carry the same lack of pity into visible damage.
branches.cn: 残忍的行为把同样的无怜悯变成看得见的伤害。

branches.en: The old carefree sense keeps the empty chest but drops the accusation.
branches.cn: 旧的「没心没肺」义项同样保留了空心画面，却不再带指责意味。

branches.en: Places and systems are judged by warmth as if they too had hearts.
branches.cn: 地方与制度也被用「是否有温度」来衡量，好像它们也有一颗心。

branches.en: A heartless person often leaves a heartless act behind.
branches.cn: 冷酷的人常常留下冷酷的行为。

intro.en: Heartless is a native English compound of heart and -less, with the family extended by -ly and -ness and related to similar -less words.
intro.cn: heartless 是英语本族语中 heart 与 -less 的组合，词族经 -ly 与 -ness 扩展，并与同类以 -less 结尾的词相关。

latinIntro.en: Heartless has no Latin ancestor, but its heart matches the Latin cor and cordis used in concord and record.
latinIntro.cn: heartless 没有拉丁语祖先，但它的 heart 对应拉丁语 cor 与 cordis，见于 concord、record 等词。

items.meaning: the heart, the seat of feeling
items.example: Heart is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: heart 是整个词族的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -less removes the heart from the picture.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 把这颗心从画面中去掉。

items.example: Heartless describes a person with no pity.
items.exampleCN: heartless 形容一个毫无怜悯的人。

items.example: The same -less builds countless, and endless, with the same lack.
items.exampleCN: 同一个 -less 也构成 countless 与 endless，表示同样的「没有」。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns heartless into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把 heartless 变成副词。

items.example: Heartlessly describes how an act was done.
items.exampleCN: heartlessly 描述一个行为是怎么做的。

items.example: The suffix -ness makes the quality a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 把这种性质变成名词。

items.example: Heartlessness names the missing heart as a quality.
items.exampleCN: heartlessness 把「缺心」当作一种性质来命名。

items.example: Hearty turns the same base toward warmth.
items.exampleCN: hearty 把同一个词根转向温情。

definition_zh: 公顷（面积单位，等于一万平方米）；公顷制下的地块面积
definition_en: a metric unit of area equal to ten thousand square metres, used especially for land
core_image: 一块边长为一百米的正方形地，一圈走下来正好四百米
scene: 农场的沙盘上，一整片保护区被画成了格子。Each coloured square on the map stands for one hectare of protected forest.
sceneCN: 这里 hectare 是「公顷」（第 1 个义项：一万平方米的面积单位）；句意：地图上每一个彩色方块代表一公顷受保护的森林。

collocations.zh: 单位面积产量；每公顷产量

derivatives.zh: 由 hectare 加 -age 构成，义为「以公顷计的田地面积」
由 hectare 的前半支撑单位 are（一百平方米）拆出：公顷本是一百个 are，而在现代英语里 are 这个单位已极少单独使用

senses.title: A unit of area for land
senses.definition: a metric unit of land area equal to ten thousand square metres, or about two and a half acres
senses.definitionCN: 公制土地面积单位，等于一万平方米，约相当于二点五英亩
senses.example: The farmer owns forty hectares of wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 这位农民拥有四十公顷小麦地。
senses.why: Hecto- means one hundred and are is a hundred square metres, so one hectare packs a hundred ares into a square of one hundred metres by one hundred metres.
senses.whyCN: hecto- 表示一百，are 是一百平方米，所以一公顷把一百个 are 装进一个边长一百米的正方形里。

senses.title: The repeated unit in land measurements
senses.definition: the counting unit used after a number in statements about crop yield, forest cover, and land prices
senses.definitionCN: 在讲产量、森林覆盖和地价时跟在数字后面反复使用的计数单位
senses.example: Rice yield rose to six tonnes per hectare.
senses.exampleCN: 稻米产量提高到每公顷六吨。
senses.why: Once the unit is fixed, people stop saying ten thousand square metres and simply count in hectares.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦固定，人们就不再念叨「一万平方米」，而是直接用公顷来数。

senses.title: A familiar picture of large area
senses.titleCN: 约一个标准草场的画面
senses.definition: an area about the size of a sports field, used as an everyday picture of how big something is
senses.definitionCN: 面积大致相当于一个标准运动场，被当作衡量面积大小的日常参照
senses.example: The new playground is nearly a hectare in size.
senses.exampleCN: 新操场面积接近一公顷。
senses.why: Because the square of one hundred metres is easy to walk and to see, the hectare becomes a mental picture and not just a number.
senses.whyCN: 因为边长一百米的正方形很好走、也很好看，公顷就成了心里的画面，而不只是一个数字。

senses.title: The unit as a policy and legal term
senses.definition: the unit used in planning rules, land registration, and environmental targets to set limits and quotas
senses.definitionCN: 用于规划规则、土地登记与环境目标中设定限值与配额的单位
senses.example: The park must protect at least one thousand hectares of wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 这个公园必须保护至少一千公顷湿地。
senses.why: Official targets need one common unit, so the hectare becomes the yardstick of policy and law.
senses.whyCN: 官方目标需要一个统一单位，公顷因此成为政策与法律的标尺。

intro.en: Hectare is a modern French coinage that joins a Greek prefix, hecto-, with a Latin area word, are.
intro.cn: hectare 是近代法语新造的词，把希腊语前缀 hecto- 与拉丁语的面积词 are 拼在一起。

items.en: Hekaton means one hundred.
items.cn: 希腊语 hekaton 意为「一百」。

items.en: The new metric system coins hectomètre with the prefix hecto- taken from hekaton.
items.cn: 新的公制体系用来自 hekaton 的前缀 hecto- 造出 hectomètre（百米）。

items.en: Area is a bare flat surface, the noun behind the older land measure are.
items.cn: 拉丁语 area 指裸露的平面，也就是较早的地积单位 are 的来源。

items.en: Hectare is formed as hecto- plus are, one hundred ares, a square of one hundred metres.
items.cn: hectare 由 hecto- 加 are 构成，即一百个 are，也就是边长一百米的正方形。

items.en: English borrows hectare and uses it for farmland, forests, and planning.
items.cn: 英语借入 hectare，用来衡量农田、森林与规划用地。

items.en: The hectare is kept as an accepted unit, equal to exactly ten thousand square metres.
items.cn: 公顷作为被接受的单位保留下来，直接规定为一万平方米。

note.en: Hectare belongs to the metric land family built on the Greek hundred and the Latin area word, and stands near the other units of land area.
note.cn: hectare 属于以希腊语「一百」和拉丁语面积词为核心的公制地积词族，并与其它土地面积单位相邻。

entries.definition: a unit of area equal to one hundred square metres
entries.definitionCN: 一百平方米的面积单位（hectare 的基单位）

entries.definition: one hundred metres
entries.definitionCN: 百米（与 hectare 共用 hecto- 前缀）

entries.definition: to bully by noisy threats
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同；hector 来自荷马史诗中的人物名

entries.definition: an older unit of land area of about four thousand square metres
entries.definitionCN: 较古老的面积单位，约四千平方米；一公顷约合二点五英亩

entries.definition: the basic metric unit of area
entries.definitionCN: 平方米；公制面积的基本单位

entries.definition: one million square metres, or one hundred hectares
entries.definitionCN: 平方公里；一百万平方米，即一百公顷

normalIntro.en: Hectare is built to be counted: a Greek hundred sitting in front of a Latin piece of flat land.
normalIntro.cn: hectare 天生就是用来数的：希腊语的「一百」站在一块拉丁语平地前面。

normal.en: Hecto- means one hundred, so one hectare holds one hundred ares.
normal.cn: hecto- 表示一百，所以一公顷装得下一百个 are。

normal.en: Most measurements use hectares after a number, as in forty hectares.
normal.cn: 大多数场合在数字后面用 hectares，比如四十公顷。

normal.en: The common partner phrase is per hectare for yield.
normal.cn: 最常见的搭配是 per hectare，用来说产量。

normal.en: Both hectare and hectometre share the hecto- prefix of one hundred.
normal.cn: hectare 与 hectometre 共用表示一百的 hecto- 前缀。

normal.en: The hectare keeps the Latin are, so it shares land with acre and area.
normal.cn: hectare 保留了拉丁语 are，因此和 acre、area 共享「平地」这一概念。

abstract.en: Picture a field one hundred paces long and one hundred paces wide.
abstract.cn: 想象一块长一百步、宽一百步的田。

abstract.en: Picture a table of yields where every row ends in the same unit.
abstract.cn: 想象一张产量表，每一行的末尾都是同一个单位。

abstract.en: Picture a stadium pitch lying inside a larger square of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一块球场草坪躺在一片更大的方形草地上。

examples.en: The estate covers some two hundred hectares of olive groves.
examples.cn: 这片庄园占地约两百公顷橄榄园。

examples.en: Farming yields per hectare have doubled in forty years.
examples.cn: 四十年里，每公顷的农业产量翻了一番。

examples.en: The council bought twelve hectares for a new park.
examples.cn: 市政会买下十二公顷土地建新公园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「赫克塔」——「赫」字很大，一大片地方覆盖在这片地上，正好一百米见方；只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hekaton（一百）→ 法语前缀 hecto-（百）+ 拉丁语 area（平面；are 百平方米）→ 法语 hectare（一百个 are）→ 英语 hectare，核心义「一百个百平方米」。

sensesIntro.en: Hectare first names the unit itself, then becomes the counting unit in measurements, then an everyday picture of area, and finally a legal and policy term.
sensesIntro.cn: hectare 先指单位本身，再成为计量时反复使用的计数单位，随后变成日常的面积画面，最后成为法规与政策用词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square field one hundred metres on each side.
core.cn: 核心意象：边长为一百米的一块正方形田地。

branches.en: The unit itself is the core sense.
branches.cn: 单位本身是核心义项。

branches.en: The unit in measurement is how the hectare is counted.
branches.cn: 作为计量单位，公顷就是这样被数出来的。

branches.en: The picture of an area is what the hectare means to the eye.
branches.cn: 面积画面是公顷留给眼睛的印象。

branches.en: The unit in law and policy is the hectare as a yardstick.
branches.cn: 在法规与政策中，公顷是一把衡量尺。

branches.en: The unit and its counting use come from the same fixed square.
branches.cn: 单位本身与计数用法都来自同一个固定的正方形。

intro.en: Hectare mixes a Greek hundred prefix with a Latin flat-surface word, with English hectare, hectares, and sibling metric units around it.
intro.cn: hectare 把希腊语的「一百」前缀与拉丁语的「平面」词拼在一起，周围有 hectare、hectares 以及同系列的公制单位。

latinIntro.en: Latin area means a bald spot or open level space, and it is the second half of hectare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 area 意为一块空地或平坦空间，它就是 hectare 的后半部分。

items.example: The prefix hecto- supplies the hundred.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 hecto- 提供「一百」这个意思。

items.example: Hekaton is the Greek source of hecto-.
items.exampleCN: hekaton 是 hecto- 的希腊语来源。

items.example: Area gives the flat land of the word.
items.exampleCN: area 提供了这个词中「平地」的部分。

items.meaning: a unit of one hundred square metres
items.example: The are is the smallest unit inside the hectare.
items.exampleCN: are 是公顷内部最小的单位。

items.meaningCN: 一百个 are；公顷的早期形式
items.example: Hectoare was the older way of naming the unit.
items.exampleCN: hectoare 是这个单位的早期叫法。

items.meaning: a unit of ten thousand square metres
items.example: Hectare is the shortened modern form.
items.exampleCN: hectare 是缩短后的现代形式。

items.example: Hectares is the plural used after numbers.
items.exampleCN: hectares 是数字后面的复数量词。

items.example: Hectarage adds -age to name a measured extent.
items.exampleCN: hectarage 加上 -age 表示被量出的一块面积。

items.example: Hectometre shares the same hundred prefix.
items.exampleCN: hectometre 共用同一个「百」前缀。

items.meaningCN: 表示集合或数量的后缀
items.example: The suffix -age makes a mass noun from a measure.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 把度量词变成集合名词。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 一百（与希腊语 hekaton 同出远古词根）

definition_zh: 忙乱的；紧张忙碌的；（旧）发热的
definition_en: full of rushed activity, pressure, and little order
core_image: 一张桌上摊满文件，手机与门铃同时响个不停
scene: 周一的编辑部里，电话、打印机和跑动的助理混成一团。It was a hectic morning in the newsroom, with every desk shouting for attention.
sceneCN: 这里 hectic 是「忙乱的」（第 1 个义项：事情挤在一起、节奏急促而混乱）；句意：新闻编辑室里那个上午忙乱不堪，每个工位都在喊人。

pos.zh: （旧）发热的；与消瘦性热病有关的

collocations.zh: 既忙乱又混乱（并列说法）

derivatives.zh: 由 hectic 加 -ly 构成，义为「忙乱地；紧张地」
由 hectic 加 -ness 构成，义为「忙乱的状态」
hectic 的旧医学搭配，指伴随消瘦与潮红的慢性发热

senses.title: Full of rushed activity
senses.definition: describing a period or place so full of rushed activity that order is hard to keep
senses.definitionCN: 形容一段时间或一个地方充满急促的活动，秩序很难维持
senses.example: The week before the exam was hectic.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前那一周忙得不可开交。
senses.why: The free spelling hectical came from Greek hektikos, meaning caused by a habit or state of the body, and English medical use tied it to a feverish condition that never settles.
senses.whyCN: 较自由的拼写 hectical 来自希腊语 hektikos（由身体的习惯或状态引起的），英语医学用法把它系在一种持续不退的热病上，于是「忙个不停、静不下来」的核心义从这里长出。

senses.title: Exciting but exhausting pace
senses.definition: fast, loud, and exciting enough to be fun for a while but tiring in the end
senses.definitionCN: 又快又闹，短时间令人兴奋，久了却让人疲惫
senses.example: They loved the hectic rhythm of festival nights.
senses.exampleCN: 他们喜欢节庆夜晚那种紧张又兴奋的节奏。
senses.why: Once the word left medicine, the fast pulse image turned into a busy rhythm that is exciting as well as tiring.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词离开医学，急促脉搏的画面就变成一种既让人兴奋又让人疲惫的忙碌节奏。

senses.title: A period under pressure
senses.definition: a specific period, such as a launch week or a holiday rush, when work or events pile up
senses.definitionCN: 特定的时间段，如发布周或节假日高峰，工作与事务堆在一起
senses.example: The launch week was the most hectic of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 发布周是一年中最忙乱的一周。
senses.why: Piled-up tasks give the abstract rush a calendar: the pressure can be named as a defined block of days.
senses.whyCN: 堆积的任务给抽象的忙乱一个日历：这种压力可以被命名成一段确定的时日。

senses.title: Relating to a wasting fever
senses.definition: in old medical writing, describing a continuing fever that accompanies wasting of the body
senses.definitionCN: 旧医学文献中，形容伴随身体消瘦的持续发热
senses.example: Older texts speak of a hectic fever and a hectic flush.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文献里提到「持续热病」和「消耗性潮红」。
senses.why: This is the original sense, and modern word lists still preserve it as the historical root of the busy sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义，现代词表仍保留它，正是「忙乱」义的来处。

intro.en: Hectic enters English from a pair of Greek medical adjectives, one of which came through Latin and French; its modern busy sense is recent.
intro.cn: hectic 从一组希腊语医学形容词进入英语，其中一个形式经过拉丁语与法语；它「忙乱」的现代义是较晚才有的。

items.en: Hektikos means habitual or from the state of the body, and describes certain fevers.
items.cn: 希腊语 hektikos 意为「习惯的、由身体状态引起的」，用于描述某些热病。

items.en: Hektikon is the neuter form, the adjective shaped as a noun and used as a medical term.
items.cn: hektikon 是其中性形式，把该形容词名词化后作医学术语。

items.en: Hectica is used for the wasting fever, and this form came through French as étique.
items.cn: 拉丁语 hectica 指消耗性热病，这一形式经法语变为 étique。

items.en: English borrows the two Greek-derived forms, giving ettique and the freer hectical.
items.cn: 英语借入两个源自希腊语的形式，得出 ettique 以及较自由的 hectical。

items.en: Hectical shortens to hectic, and the word starts meaning busy, flushed, and feverish in everyday speech.
items.cn: hectical 缩为 hectic，这个词在日常话语里开始表示「忙乱、满脸涨红、像发烧一样」。

items.en: Today hectic overwhelmingly means frantic and busy, while the fever sense survives only in old texts.
items.cn: 如今 hectic 绝大多数时候表示「忙乱不堪」，发热义只留在旧文本里。

note.en: Hectic keeps a Greek medical past inside its busy modern sense, and stands near words for fever and for a rushing life.
note.cn: hectic 在忙乱的现代义里藏着希腊医学的旧身世，并与表示发热、忙碌生活的词相邻。

entries.definition: the earlier, freer form of the same adjective
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词较早、较自由的拼写形式

entries.definition: to bully by noisy threats
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同；hector 来自荷马史诗中的人物名

entries.definition: the red flushed face of a wasting fever
entries.definitionCN: 消耗性热病时脸上出现的潮红

entries.definition: wildly hurried and lacking calm
entries.definitionCN: 发狂似的匆忙；忙乱到失去冷静

entries.definition: showing the restlessness of a fever
entries.definitionCN: 发着烧似的；躁动不安的

entries.definition: in a state of complete disorder
entries.definitionCN: 极度混乱的；毫无秩序的

normalIntro.en: Hectic is a fever word that cooled into a busy word, and the feverish pulse is still inside its modern picture.
normalIntro.cn: hectic 是一个从发热词冷却成忙碌词的例子，而「发烧般的脉搏」仍留在它的现代画面里。

normal.en: Hectic started as a medical word for a wasting fever connected to the Greek root hektikos.
normal.cn: hectic 起初是医学词，指消耗性热病，源头是希腊语 hektikos。

normal.en: The earlier spelling hectical shows the adjective came in through the Greek-derived neuter form.
normal.cn: 较早的拼写 hectical 说明这个形容词是从希腊语来源的中性形式进来的。

normal.en: The common partner is schedule, as in a hectic schedule.
normal.cn: 最常见的搭配词是 schedule，如 a hectic schedule。

normal.en: Compare frantic and chaotic: frantic is a frantic state of mind, chaotic is disorder, hectic is mostly a busy pace.
normal.cn: 对比 frantic 与 chaotic：frantic 多指人的慌乱，chaotic 指秩序混乱，hectic 主要指节奏忙碌。

normal.en: Do not confuse hectic with hector: hector is a name from Greek story, so the two are not related.
normal.cn: 不要把 hectic 和 hector 混为一谈：hector 是希腊故事里的名字，并非同源。

abstract.en: Picture a desk covered with papers while two phones ring at once.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上摊满文件，两部电话同时响着。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded fair with music, shouting, and people rushing everywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象热闹的集市，音乐、叫喊和四处奔走的人混在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of the launch week piling taller than any other week.
abstract.cn: 想象发布周的任务柱状图，比其它任何一周都高。

examples.en: The days before the wedding were hectic from sunrise to dark.
examples.cn: 婚礼前那几天从早到晚都忙得团团转。

examples.en: She enjoys the hectic pace of the restaurant kitchen.
examples.cn: 她喜欢餐厅厨房那种紧张忙碌的节奏。

examples.en: Things got hectic when the guests arrived two hours early.
examples.cn: 客人提前两小时到的时候，事情一下子乱成一团。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「赫克提克」——听起来像医院里护士一路小跑、嘴里还念着名字的紧张样子；只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hektikos（习惯的；由身体状态引起的）与其中性形式 hektikon → 拉丁语 hectica（消耗性热病）→ 英语 ettique、hectical → 缩略为 hectic，核心义「持续发热→忙乱不息」。

sensesIntro.en: Hectic begins as a fever that will not settle, becomes a rushed pace, then a period under pressure, and keeps its medical sense only in old texts.
sensesIntro.cn: hectic 从一种不肯退下去的发热开始，变为急促的节奏，再指压力下的忙碌时段，而医学义只留在旧文本里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every bell ringing at once in a room that cannot keep up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间屋子里所有铃同时响起，根本应付不过来。

branches.en: The busy day is the ordinary sense.
branches.cn: 忙碌的一天是日常义项。

branches.en: An exciting fast rhythm is the pleasant side of the same rush.
branches.cn: 令人兴奋的快节奏是这种忙乱讨喜的一面。

branches.en: A pressured week is the busy day put on a calendar.
branches.cn: 压力周就是把忙碌的一天放到日历上。

branches.en: The fever sense is the old medical root of the word.
branches.cn: 发热义是这个词的旧医学根。

branches.en: A busy place and a busy week share the same lacked order.
branches.cn: 忙乱的地方与忙乱的一周同样缺的都是秩序。

intro.en: Hectic has few English affixes, but its family shows how a Greek adjective became a modern busy word, with old relatives like ettique around it.
intro.cn: hectic 的构词部件很少，但这个词族展示了希腊语形容词如何变成现代的「忙碌」词，周围还有 ettique 这样的旧血缘词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin step was hectica, a fever word from Greek, and -ic in English repeats the form of the original adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语这一步是 hectica（来自希腊语的发热词），英语中的 -ic 则重复了原形容词的形式。

items.meaningCN: 习惯的；由身体状态引起的
items.example: Hektikos describes a fever that follows the habit of the body.
items.exampleCN: hektikos 描述一种跟着身体惯性走的发热。

items.meaning: the habitual, used as a noun
items.example: Hektikon gives English the earlier hectical.
items.exampleCN: hektikon 给英语带来较早的 hectical。

items.example: Hectica is the Latin medical form.
items.exampleCN: hectica 是拉丁语的医学形式。

items.example: French étique travels beside the word.
items.exampleCN: 法语 étique 与这个词同行。

items.example: Ettique is the oldest form borrowed into English.
items.exampleCN: ettique 是借入英语的最早形式。

items.example: Hectical is the free spelling that later shortened.
items.exampleCN: hectical 是后来被缩短的自由拼写。

items.example: Hectic is the short form used today.
items.exampleCN: hectic 是今天使用的短形式。

items.example: The suffix -ic marks an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 标记一个表示关系的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly builds hectically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 hectically。

items.example: Hectically describes how the day passed.
items.exampleCN: hectically 描述这一天是怎么过的。

definition_zh: 百帕，气压单位，等于一百帕斯卡；常用于天气预报中的气压播报
definition_en: a unit of pressure equal to one hundred pascals, used especially in weather reports
core_image: 气压表上缓慢转动的指针，旁边标着一个百帕刻度
scene: 气象播报员指着云图说，海面气压正在快速下降，并用百帕报告读数。The weather presenter pointed at the cloud map and reported the sea level pressure in hectopascals.
sceneCN: 这里 hectopascal 是「气压单位」（第 1 个义项：百帕）；句意：气象播报员指着云图说，海面气压正在快速下降，并以百帕为单位报出读数。

pos.zh: 百帕（气压单位，等于一百帕斯卡）

collocations.zh: 每小时百帕数，描述气压变化速度

derivatives.zh: 帕斯卡，由 hecto- 所修饰的基本压力单位
表示「一百」的构词前缀，来自希腊语 hekaton
千帕，由 kilo-（一千）加 pascal 构成
毫巴，旧式气压单位，数值上等于百帕

senses.title: The scientific pressure unit
senses.definition: a unit of pressure equal to one hundred pascals
senses.definitionCN: 等于一百帕斯卡的压力单位
senses.example: One hectopascal is exactly one hundred pascals.
senses.exampleCN: 一帕斯卡乘以一百正好是一个百帕。
senses.why: The prefix hecto- marks a hundred, so the name simply means a hundred pascals.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 hecto- 表示「一百」，所以这个名字的字面意思就是一百个帕斯卡。

senses.title: The weather report unit
senses.definition: the unit in which weather forecasts announce air pressure
senses.definitionCN: 天气预报中用来播报气压的单位
senses.example: Pressure at the coast was near a thousand and ten hectopascals.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海地区的气压接近一千零一十百帕。
senses.why: Atmospheric pressure naturally sits in the thousand mark, so meteorologists prefer this hundred-based unit over the tiny pascal.
senses.whyCN: 大气压自然落在一千上下，气象学家因此偏爱这个以百为进位的单位，而不愿用细小的帕斯卡。

senses.title: The standard chart unit
senses.definition: the unit printed on synoptic charts and weather maps
senses.definitionCN: 天气图和天气图上标注的数值单位
senses.example: Each line on the chart joins points of equal hectopascals.
senses.exampleCN: 图上的每条线都连接气压值相同的点。
senses.why: When many stations are compared on one map, a hundred-sized unit keeps the numbers short and readable.
senses.whyCN: 在同一张图上比较许多观测站时，以百为单位的刻度能让数字简短易读。

senses.title: The change indicator
senses.definition: the unit used to describe how quickly pressure rises or falls
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述气压上升或下降快慢的单位
senses.example: The storm deepened by ten hectopascals in a single day.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴在一天之内加深了十百帕。
senses.why: Because storms are tracked by pressure change, the unit becomes a way of measuring how fast the weather system is growing.
senses.whyCN: 由于风暴靠气压变化来追踪，这个单位就成了衡量天气系统增强速度的方式。

senses.title: The alternative to millibar
senses.definition: the modern name for a number that older charts wrote as millibars
senses.definitionCN: 旧图以毫巴标注、如今改用百帕的同一个数值
senses.example: The old millibar value equals the same amount of hectopascals.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的毫巴数值与相同数量的百帕完全相等。
senses.why: Meteorology switched from the bar-based millibar to the pascal-based unit, yet the numbers stayed exactly the same.
senses.whyCN: 气象学从基于巴的毫巴改用基于帕斯卡的单位，可数字却完全没变。

intro.en: Hectopascal joins Greek hekaton, meaning a hundred, with pascal, the pressure unit named after the scientist Blaise Pascal.
intro.cn: hectopascal 由希腊语 hekaton（一百）与 pascal 合成，后者是以科学家帕斯卡命名的压力单位。

items.en: Hekaton means one hundred.
items.cn: 希腊语 hekaton 意为一百。

items.en: The metric system sets the prefix hecto- for a hundred.
items.cn: 公制确立 hecto- 为表示一百的前缀。

items.en: The pascal is named after Blaise Pascal as the unit of pressure.
items.cn: 帕斯卡作为压力单位，以布莱士·帕斯卡之名命名。

items.en: Weather services adopt the hectopascal to replace the millibar.
items.cn: 各国气象部门采用百帕，取代毫巴。

items.en: Hectopascal appears on charts, forecasts, and barometers.
items.cn: hectopascal 出现在天气图、预报和气压表上。

note.en: Hectopascal sits in a family of pressure units: pascal, bar, millibar, and kilopascal.
note.cn: hectopascal 属于压力单位家族，与帕斯卡、巴、毫巴、千帕相邻。

entries.definition: the SI unit of pressure
entries.definitionCN: 帕斯卡，国际单位制中的压力单位

entries.definition: a thousand pascals
entries.definitionCN: 千帕，等于一千帕斯卡

entries.definition: a hundred metres
entries.definitionCN: 百米，共享表示一百的前缀

entries.definition: an old unit of pressure, equal in value to a hectopascal
entries.definitionCN: 毫巴，旧式气压单位，数值上等于百帕

entries.definition: an instrument that measures air pressure
entries.definitionCN: 气压表

entries.definition: a line on a map joining places of equal pressure
entries.definitionCN: 等压线，连接气压相同地点的线

normalIntro.en: Hectopascal is a hundred pascals, and the hundred is the whole trick of the word.
normalIntro.cn: hectopascal 就是一百帕斯卡，而「百」正是这个词的记忆钥匙。

normal.en: Hecto- means a hundred, as in hectometre and hectolitre.
normal.cn: hecto- 表示「一百」， hectometre 与 hectolitre 里也是这个意思。

normal.en: Pascal honours the scientist Blaise Pascal, the pioneer of pressure studies.
normal.cn: pascal 纪念研究压力的先驱科学家布莱士·帕斯卡。

normal.en: One hectopascal equals one millibar, so the two words often replace each other.
normal.cn: 一个百帕等于一个毫巴，所以两个词常能互相替换。

normal.en: Forecasts say a pressure of around a thousand and thirteen hectopascals at sea level.
normal.cn: 预报常说海平面气压约为一千零一十三百帕。

normal.en: Think of the common barometer dial whose numbers run in steps of a hundred.
normal.cn: 想想常见的气压表盘，刻度正以百为单位递进。

abstract.en: Picture a jar holding a hundred tiny pressure stones labelled pascal.
abstract.cn: 想象一只罐子里装着一百颗写着 pascal 的小压力石子。

abstract.en: Imagine a weather map with a big number like a thousand printed in the centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，中央印着一个上千的大数字。

abstract.en: See a single neat line running across the map, joining every place with the same reading.
abstract.cn: 想象一条整洁的线横穿全图，把读数相同的地方连在一起。

examples.en: Air pressure at sea level is roughly a thousand and thirteen hectopascals.
examples.cn: 海平面的气压大约是一千零一十三百帕。

examples.en: The meteorologist reported a drop of eight hectopascals overnight.
examples.cn: 气象学家报告夜间气压下降了八百帕。

examples.en: Older maps still print millibars where new charts print hectopascals.
examples.cn: 旧地图上仍印毫巴，而新图表则印百帕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海克托帕」——可以想象「海」面气压「克」服了「帕」斯卡的细小刻度，只好用百帕来报数；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hekaton（一百）→ 公制前缀 hecto-（百）+ 以科学家帕斯卡命名的 pascal（帕斯卡单位）→ 英语 hectopascal，核心义「以百为进位的压力单位」。

sensesIntro.en: Hectopascal begins as a plain hundred-pascal unit, moves into weather reports, charts, and storm tracking, and finally replaces the older millibar.
sensesIntro.cn: hectopascal 先是纯粹的一百帕斯卡单位，再走进天气预报、天气图与风暴追踪，最后取代了旧的毫巴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a barometer needle beside a hundred-step scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：气压表指针旁一道以百为进位的刻度。

branches.en: The scientific unit is simply a hundred pascals.
branches.cn: 科学义项就是一百个帕斯卡。

branches.en: Weather forecasts speak of pressure in these units.
branches.cn: 天气预报用这个单位播报气压。

branches.en: Charts print the same unit beside each station.
branches.cn: 天气图在每个观测站旁印上同一种单位。

branches.en: Storms are tracked by how fast the reading changes.
branches.cn: 风暴靠读数变化的速度来追踪。

branches.en: The new unit carries the same value as the old millibar.
branches.cn: 新单位与旧毫巴承载着相同的数值。

intro.en: Hectopascal is a metric compound: the prefix hecto- sits before the unit pascal.
intro.cn: hectopascal 是公制合成词：前缀 hecto- 位于单位 pascal 之前。

latinIntro.en: The prefix comes from Greek through French metric usage; pascal is a scientific surname used as a unit.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀经法语公制用法来自希腊语；pascal 则是用作单位名称的科学家族姓氏。

items.example: The prefix hecto- marks a hundredfold amount.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 hecto- 表示一百倍。

items.example: A pascal is a force of one newton on one square metre.
items.exampleCN: 一帕斯卡就是一平方米上的一牛顿力。

items.example: The compound locks the two parts together.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词把两部分牢牢结合起来。

items.example: The prefix kilo- forms kilopascal.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 kilo- 构成 kilopascal。

items.example: Kilopascal suits larger pressure figures.
items.exampleCN: kilopascal 适合表示较大的压力数值。

items.example: The prefix milli- forms millibar.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 milli- 构成 millibar。

items.example: Millibar is the older pressure unit.
items.exampleCN: millibar 是更早的压力单位。

items.example: The form baro- shapes barometer and isobar.
items.exampleCN: 组合形式 baro- 构成 barometer 与 isobar。

items.example: Barometer combines weight and measure.
items.exampleCN: barometer 把「重量」与「测量」组合起来。

definition_zh: 不加注意的；掉以轻心的；不管不顾的
definition_en: not paying attention to something, especially a risk or a warning
core_image: 一个人边走边看手机，完全没看见脚边的水坑
scene: 大雨过后路面湿滑，行人却仍边走边打电话。The young man walked past the warning sign, heedless of the wet floor and the people behind him.
sceneCN: 这里 heedless 是「不加注意的」（第 1 个义项：对提醒和危险毫无注意）；句意：这个年轻男子走过警示牌，对湿滑的地面和身后的人全然不顾。

pos.zh: 不加注意的；掉以轻心的；不管不顾的

derivatives.zh: heed 去掉否定后缀 -less 得到的基础动词，意为「注意；留心」
heed 加 -ful（充满）构成，意为「留心的」，与 heedless 语义相反
heedless 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，意为「粗心；不留意」
heedless 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，意为「不加注意地」

senses.title: Not taking notice
senses.definition: paying no attention to something that really deserves it
senses.definitionCN: 对理应注意到的事物毫不在意
senses.example: He was heedless of the traffic as he crossed the road.
senses.exampleCN: 他过马路时全然不理会来往车辆。
senses.why: The suffix -less turns heed, to pay attention, into a simple absence: there is no attention at all.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -less 把表示「留心」的 heed 变成一种缺席：注意完全不存在。

senses.title: Ignoring danger or warning
senses.definition: going ahead while ignoring a clear risk or a warning
senses.definitionCN: 无视明显的风险或警告继续行事
senses.example: The team was heedless of the storm warning and set out anyway.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍无视风暴预警，照样出发了。
senses.why: Once attention is missing, the object that is missed is most often a danger, so the word fixes on reckless disregard.
senses.whyCN: 一旦注意缺席，缺席的对象往往就是危险，于是这个词固定为「莽撞地不管不顾」。

senses.title: Careless and thoughtless
senses.definition: acting in a careless way that brings harm or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 行为轻率，带来危害或麻烦
senses.example: Her heedless spending left the family in debt.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻率的开销让家里背上了债。
senses.why: Lack of attention grows into a character trait, describing a person who acts first and thinks later.
senses.whyCN: 注意的缺失延伸成一种性格特征，用来形容先行动、后思考的人。

senses.title: Unmindful of feelings
senses.definition: giving no thought to other people and their feelings
senses.definitionCN: 丝毫不顾及他人及其感受
senses.example: He was heedless of how his words hurt his sister.
senses.exampleCN: 他完全没顾及自己的话伤了妹妹。
senses.why: The same absence of heed can point at people rather than at objects, giving a social and emotional sense.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「不留心」也可以指向人而不是物，于是生出社交与情感层面的意思。

senses.title: Not caring about reputation
senses.definition: showing no concern for what other people think of one
senses.definitionCN: 毫不在意旁人对自己的看法
senses.example: The singer was heedless of public opinion and kept touring.
senses.exampleCN: 这位歌手不在乎公众舆论，继续巡演。
senses.why: Because heed also means to look after or preserve, a heedless person fails to guard even a reputation.
senses.whyCN: 因为 heed 还有「照看、保住」之义，heedless 的人连名声也不去守护。

senses.title: Literary: rushing on without care
senses.titleCN: 书面语：无所顾忌地奔向前
senses.definition: moving with energy while ignoring everything around
senses.definitionCN: 只顾往前，无视周围一切
senses.example: The heedless river tore through the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 那奔涌的河水毫无顾忌地冲过山谷。
senses.why: Writers extend the human absence of care to natural forces that sweep ahead without restraint.
senses.whyCN: 写作者把人类身上「不留意」的特质扩展到自然界，用来形容毫无约束向前冲刷的力量。

intro.en: Heedless is the English word heed with the native suffix -less, meaning without. Heed itself comes from Old English hedan, to take care of.
intro.cn: heedless 由英语词 heed 加本族后缀 -less（没有）构成；heed 本身来自古英语 hedan，意为照看。

items.en: Hedan means to take care of or attend to.
items.cn: 古英语 hedan 意为照看、留意。

items.en: Heed becomes both a verb and a noun of attention.
items.cn: heed 既作动词也作名词，表示注意。

items.en: The suffix -less is added, giving heedless as without heeding.
items.cn: 加上后缀 -less，构成 heedless，意为「不留意」。

items.en: Poets use heedless for swift rivers and racing clouds.
items.cn: 诗人们用 heedless 形容奔涌的河流与飞驰的云。

items.en: The adverb heedlessly and the noun heedlessness settle the family.
items.cn: 副词 heedlessly 与名词 heedlessness 让这个词族定型。

note.en: Heedless is built from heed plus the private suffix -less, close to heed, heedful, and to careless or reckless.
note.cn: heedless 由 heed 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，与 heed、heedful 以及 careless、reckless 相邻。

entries.definition: to pay attention to
entries.definitionCN: 留意；注意

entries.definition: paying careful attention
entries.definitionCN: 留心的；小心的

entries.definition: not necessary
entries.definitionCN: 不必要的，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: not giving enough attention and so making mistakes
entries.definitionCN: 粗心的；不小心的

entries.definition: acting without thinking about danger
entries.definitionCN: 鲁莽的；不顾危险的

entries.definition: not paying proper attention
entries.definitionCN: 不专心的；不注意的

normalIntro.en: Heedless is heed plus less: less attention, no attention at all.
normalIntro.cn: heedless 就是 heed 加 less：注意更少，直到完全没有。

normal.en: Heed means attention, and -less means without.
normal.cn: heed 意为注意，-less 意为没有。

normal.en: The usual pattern is heedless of something, as in heedless of danger.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 heedless of 加名词，例如 heedless of danger。

normal.en: Compare heedful: heedful people notice, heedless people do not.
normal.cn: 对比 heedful：留心的人会注意，heedless 的人则不会。

normal.en: The adverb is heedlessly, the noun is heedlessness.
normal.cn: 它的副词是 heedlessly，名词是 heedlessness。

normal.en: Do not confuse heedless with needless, from need; they share only the ending.
normal.cn: 别把 heedless 和来自 need 的 needless 混淆，二者只是词尾相同。

abstract.en: Picture a man walking with his eyes on his phone past a puddle.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人低头看手机，走过水坑都没发现。

abstract.en: See someone stepping over a fence at the edge of a cliff.
abstract.cn: 想象有人抬脚跨过悬崖边上的护栏。

abstract.en: Imagine a shopper swiping a card without looking at the price.
abstract.cn: 想象顾客刷卡时连价格都不看一眼。

examples.en: She was heedless of the warnings on the medicine bottle.
examples.cn: 她对药瓶上的警告毫不在意。

examples.en: Heedless drivers cause many accidents on this road.
examples.cn: 粗心的司机在这条路上造成许多事故。

examples.en: The boy ran heedlessly into the street.
examples.cn: 男孩不顾一切地冲进街道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑灯了」——黑灯瞎火看不见，只好 heed + less，什么都不留意；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hedan（照看、留意）→ heed（注意）→ heed + -less（无）→ 英语 heedless，核心义「不留心」。

sensesIntro.en: Heedless starts from the plain absence of attention, then narrows to ignoring danger, and widens to carelessness, social insensitivity, and literary rushing.
sensesIntro.cn: heedless 从注意的缺席出发，先收窄为无视危险，再扩展到轻率、不顾他人感受以及书面语中的奔涌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker who never looks down at the puddle.
core.cn: 核心意象：走路的人始终没低头看一眼水坑。

branches.en: The plain sense is simply not paying attention.
branches.cn: 基本义项就是纯粹的「不留心」。

branches.en: The missed thing is often a warning or a risk.
branches.cn: 被漏掉的对象常常是警告或风险。

branches.en: Repeated inattention becomes a careless character.
branches.cn: 反复的不留神沉淀为轻率的性格。

branches.en: The same absence of care turns towards people and to public opinion.
branches.cn: 同样的不在意转向他人和公众舆论。

branches.en: Poets give the same heedlessness to rivers and storms.
branches.cn: 诗人把这种无所顾忌赋予河流与风暴。

intro.en: Heedless follows the common English pattern of base word plus the private suffix -less.
intro.cn: heedless 遵循英语中常见的构词方式：基础词加表示否定的后缀 -less。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer here: the base comes from Old English and the private suffix is native too.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语层次：词干来自古英语，否定后缀同样是本族语素。

items.example: Hedan carries a sense of guarding.
items.exampleCN: hedan 带有守护的意味。

items.example: Heed gives the base meaning of attention.
items.exampleCN: heed 提供了「注意」的核心义。

items.example: The suffix -less works without any prefixes.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 无需任何前缀即可使用。

items.example: Heedless states a total absence of attention.
items.exampleCN: heedless 表示注意完全缺席。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms heedful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 heedful。

items.example: Heedful is the opposite of heedless.
items.exampleCN: heedful 是 heedless 的反义词。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness forms heedlessness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 heedlessness。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms heedlessly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 heedlessly。

items.example: The old verb behold also reflects the heed root.
items.exampleCN: 古英语动词 behold 也映照出 heed 这一词根。

definition_zh: 增高；加强；加剧；使更强烈
definition_en: to make something greater, stronger, or more intense in degree or feeling
core_image: 一盏灯被慢慢往上推，周围的光一点点变亮
scene: 比赛只剩最后几分钟，球场的欢呼声一浪高过一浪。As the score drew level, the tension in the stadium began to heighten with every second.
sceneCN: 这里 heighten 是「加剧、使更强烈」（第 1 个义项：程度或感受变强）；句意：比分追平后，球场里的紧张气氛随着每一秒不断加剧。

derivatives.zh: heighten 减去动词后缀 -en 得到的基础名词，意为「高度」
过去分词用作形容词，意为「增强的；加剧的」
现在分词转作名词，意为「增强；加剧」

senses.title: To make stronger or more intense
senses.definition: to make a feeling, effect, or quality greater in degree
senses.definitionCN: 使感受、效果或品质在程度上变得更强
senses.example: The slow music heightened the sadness of the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 舒缓的音乐加深了这一幕的悲伤。
senses.why: Heighten comes from height plus the verb ending -en, so raising the level of a thing raises the strength of it too.
senses.whyCN: heighten 由 height 加动词后缀 -en 构成，把某物抬到更高的位置，也就把它的强度抬高了。

senses.title: To make physically higher
senses.definition: to raise something to a greater physical height
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的实际高度提高
senses.example: The builders heightened the wall around the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们加高了花园四周的墙。
senses.why: This is the most literal sense, where the idea of height is a real distance measured upwards.
senses.whyCN: 这是最本义的义项，「高度」就是朝上量出的真实距离。

senses.title: To become stronger
senses.definition: to grow more intense without an outside agent doing it
senses.definitionCN: 无需外部推动而自身变得更强
senses.example: Fear of job losses heightened as the factory closed.
senses.exampleCN: 随着工厂关闭，对失业的恐惧日益加剧。
senses.why: The verb can work without an object, since a feeling can rise by itself just as a level rises.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以不带宾语，因为感受也能像水位一样自己上涨。

senses.title: To sharpen contrast or colour
senses.definition: to make a colour, contrast, or difference stronger
senses.definitionCN: 使色彩、对比或差异更加鲜明
senses.example: The dark frame heightened the glow of the painting.
senses.exampleCN: 深色画框让画作的光泽更突出。
senses.why: In art and design, raising one quality makes the difference it creates more visible.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术与设计中，抬升一种特质，就会让它造成的差异更显眼。

senses.title: To add value or importance
senses.definition: to raise the value, status, or importance of something
senses.definitionCN: 提高某事物的价值、地位或重要性
senses.example: His years abroad heightened the value of his experience.
senses.exampleCN: 几年海外经历提升了他经验的价值。
senses.why: A higher place on a scale of worth becomes this abstract sense of a higher value.
senses.whyCN: 在价值尺度上占据更高的位置，就化为这种抽象的价值提升。

senses.title: To make sharper in awareness or reaction
senses.definition: to make someone notice or react more sharply
senses.definitionCN: 使某人更敏锐地察觉或反应
senses.example: Lack of sleep can heighten your senses and your fear.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足会让你的感官和恐惧都变得更敏锐。
senses.why: When arousal rises, attention grows keener, so the same upward movement shows as sharper perception.
senses.whyCN: 当唤醒水平升高，注意力也会更敏锐，于是同样的「上升」表现为知觉更灵敏。

senses.title: To increase risk or likelihood
senses.definition: to make a danger or chance more likely
senses.definitionCN: 使危险或可能性更容易发生
senses.example: Heavy traffic heightens the chance of an accident.
senses.exampleCN: 交通拥堵增加了发生事故的几率。
senses.why: In reports of safety and statistics, raising a figure means making the outcome more probable.
senses.whyCN: 在安全与统计报告中，把数字抬高，就等于让结果更容易发生。

intro.en: Heighten is formed inside English from height plus the verb suffix -en. Height comes from Old English hiehthu, shaped in the Middle Ages by words such as high.
intro.cn: heighten 是在英语内部由 height 加动词后缀 -en 构成的；height 来自古英语 hiehthu，在中古英语时期受 high 等词的影响定型。

items.en: Hiehthu means height or summit.
items.cn: 古英语 hiehthu 意为高度、高处。

items.en: The noun is reshaped and is also written as heighth.
items.cn: 这个名词被重新塑形，也曾写作 heighth。

items.en: Heighten appears as height plus the verb ending -en.
items.cn: 十六世纪出现 heighten，即 height 加动词词尾 -en。

items.en: Writers start using heighten for feelings and drama.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，作家用 heighten 形容情感与戏剧效果。

items.en: Heightened becomes a common adjective in news and essays.
items.cn: 现代英语中 heightened 成为新闻与文章中常见的形容词。

note.en: Heighten belongs to the height family and pairs with raise, increase, and intensify.
note.cn: heighten 属于 height 词族，与 raise、increase、intensify 相邻。

entries.definition: the distance from the bottom to the top
entries.definitionCN: 高度

entries.definition: reaching far upwards
entries.definitionCN: 高的

entries.definition: high places or peaks
entries.definitionCN: 高处；高峰

entries.definition: to become or make stronger
entries.definitionCN: 加强；强化

entries.definition: to become or make larger in amount
entries.definitionCN: 增加；增多

entries.definition: to become or make deeper
entries.definitionCN: 加深

normalIntro.en: Heighten is height turned into an action: to send something up a level.
normalIntro.cn: heighten 就是把 height 变成动作：把某物抬高一档。

normal.en: Drop the -en from heighten and you get height.
normal.cn: 把 heighten 末尾的 -en 去掉，就得到 height。

normal.en: The pattern is heighten plus the thing that grows, as in heighten tension.
normal.cn: 常见结构是 heighten 加变强的事物，例如 heighten tension。

normal.en: Compare strengthen and lengthen: -en verbs all mean to make more of something.
normal.cn: 对比 strengthen 与 lengthen：-en 动词都表示使某性质增强。

normal.en: The adjective heightened is very common in news writing.
normal.cn: 形容词 heightened 在新闻报道中非常常见。

normal.en: The silent gh of height is kept in heighten, so the spelling follows the noun.
normal.cn: height 中不发音的 gh 被保留在 heighten 里，拼写跟随名词。

abstract.en: Picture a dimmer switch being turned up until the room glows.
abstract.cn: 想象调光开关被拧大，房间渐渐发光。

abstract.en: See a tower being built one floor higher than before.
abstract.cn: 想象一座塔在原有基础上又加高了一层。

abstract.en: Imagine a heartbeat speeding up as the film reaches its climax.
abstract.cn: 想象电影走向高潮时，心跳越来越快。

examples.en: The music heightened the tension in the final scene.
examples.cn: 音乐让最后一幕的紧张气氛更加强烈。

examples.en: Heavy rain heightened the risk of flooding in the valley.
examples.cn: 大雨提高了山谷发生洪水的风险。

examples.en: Her fear heightened as the plane began to shake.
examples.cn: 飞机开始颠簸，她的恐惧也越来越重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「High 登」——高高地登上去，高度与强度都升起来了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hiehthu（高度）→ height（高度）→ height + -en（动词化）→ 英语 heighten，核心义「往上抬、变强」。

sensesIntro.en: Heighten runs from the concrete raising of a wall to stronger feelings, sharper colour, higher value, keener senses, and greater risk.
sensesIntro.cn: heighten 从实实在在地加高一面墙，延伸到情感变强、色彩变鲜明、价值提高、感官变敏锐以及风险增大。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp pushed slowly upwards until the room is bright.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯被缓缓推高，房间越来越亮。

branches.en: The main sense makes feelings and effects stronger.
branches.cn: 主要义项让情感与效果更有力。

branches.en: The literal sense raises a physical object.
branches.cn: 本义义项抬高的是实在物体。

branches.en: The intransitive sense lets the intensity rise by itself.
branches.cn: 不及物义项让强度自行上涨。

branches.en: Sharper colour and sharper senses both raise perceived intensity.
branches.cn: 更鲜明的色彩和更敏锐的感官都抬升了被感知的强度。

branches.en: Value and risk are both scales that go up.
branches.cn: 价值与风险都是可以往上升的刻度。

intro.en: Heighten follows the English verb-making suffix -en, as in strengthen, lengthen, and widen.
intro.cn: heighten 使用英语中构成动词的后缀 -en，如 strengthen、lengthen、widen。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved: height is Old English and -en is a native English suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语成分：height 是古英语词，-en 是本族英语后缀。

items.example: Hiehthu is the oldest form of the noun.
items.exampleCN: hiehthu 是这个名词最早的形式。

items.example: Height keeps a silent gh in the spelling.
items.exampleCN: height 在拼写中保留了不发音的 gh。

items.example: The suffix -en turns a word into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -en 把一个词变成动词。

items.example: Heighten moves from space to feeling.
items.exampleCN: heighten 从空间走向感受。

items.example: Strengthen shares the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: strengthen 使用同样的构词方式。

items.example: Lengthen is built on length.
items.exampleCN: lengthen 以 length 为基础。

items.example: Frighten adds -en to fright.
items.exampleCN: frighten 是在 fright 上加 -en。

items.example: Widen is built on wide.
items.exampleCN: widen 以 wide 为基础。

items.example: Heightened is formed with the -ed ending.
items.exampleCN: heightened 由 -ed 词尾构成。

definition_en: a person who has the legal right to receive the property or title of another person when that person dies
core_image: 老宅门前的一把钥匙：钥匙还没交到年轻人手里，名字早已写在遗嘱上
scene: 律师在家族群里通知，祖父留下的大宅归刚成年的长孙继承。The lawyer informed the family that the eldest grandson was the sole heir to the manor.
sceneCN: 这里 heir 是「继承人」（第 1 个义项：依法继承财产或头衔的人）；句意：律师告诉家人，长孙是这座庄园的唯一继承人。

collocations.zh: 法定继承人；确定接任者

derivatives.zh: 女继承人，由 heir 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成
继承权；继承者身份，由 heir 加抽象名词后缀 -ship 构成
无继承人的，由 heir 加否定后缀 -less 构成
传家宝，由 heir 与 loome（旧义「器具」）复合而成

senses.title: Someone who inherits property or a title
senses.definition: a person who is entitled by law or custom to receive money, land, or a title from a relative when that relative dies
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律或习俗，在亲属去世后有权获得其财产、地产或头衔的人
senses.example: As the eldest son, he was the sole heir to the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 作为长子，他是这份家产的唯一继承人。
senses.why: The Latin source heres simply means an heir or a person left behind to take the property, and that original legal sense stays at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 heres 直接就是「继承人」，指被留下接管财产的人，这个最初的法律义一直在词义中心。

senses.title: The legal heir to a parent kingdom or office
senses.titleCN: 王位继承人；法定承袭者
senses.definition: a person next in line to take over a throne, an office, or a leadership role, often by birth order
senses.definitionCN: 按出身顺序排在其次、即将接掌王位、公职或领导职位的人
senses.example: The young prince is the heir to the throne.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻的王子是王位继承人。
senses.why: Kings, titles, and offices are passed down like property, so the property sense easily extends to any position that is handed on to a successor.
senses.whyCN: 王位、头衔与职务像财产一样往下传，所以「财产」这一义很容易延伸到任何传给继任者的位置。

senses.title: A successor to an idea or tradition
senses.definition: a person or group that continues the work, ideas, or traditions of an earlier person or group
senses.definitionCN: 延续前人工作、思想或传统的人或群体
senses.example: This young writer is the heir to a long comic tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻作家是一脉悠长的喜剧传统的传承者。
senses.why: When culture is treated as an inheritance, whoever carries it on steps into the role of an heir even without any money changing hands.
senses.whyCN: 当文化被看作一份遗产时，接手延续的人即使没有金钱往来，也进入了「继承人」的角色。

senses.title: A result or effect inherited from the past
senses.titleCN: 继承而来的东西；受遗传影响者
senses.definition: something, such as a problem, a disease, or a habit, that comes down to a person or group from earlier generations
senses.definitionCN: 从上一辈留给某人或某群体的问题、疾病或习惯等
senses.example: The factory shut down, so the town was an heir to long years of unemployment.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关停，于是这座小镇继承了多年的失业问题。
senses.why: The image of a will being read can be stretched to anything passed down without being chosen, which turns the word into a metaphor for inherited burdens.
senses.whyCN: 「宣读遗嘱」的画面可以拉伸到任何不由自己选择就被传下来的东西，于是这个词成了「继承来的负担」的隐喻。

intro.en: Heir goes back to Latin heres, an heir or a person left behind to take the estate; the h was added in English in imitation of Latin spelling.
intro.cn: heir 源于拉丁语 heres（继承人、留下来接收遗产的人）；英语后来仿照拉丁拼写加上了不发音的 h。

items.en: Heres means an heir, one who takes the property of the dead.
items.cn: heres 意为继承人，即接收死者财产的人。

items.en: The adjective hereditarius, meaning hereditary, grows from the same stem.
items.cn: 意为「遗传的、世袭的」形容词 hereditarius 与它同出一源。

items.en: Old French heir keeps the same meaning and loses the Latin ending.
items.cn: 古法语 heir 保留了相同含义，只去掉了拉丁语词尾。

items.en: Middle English adopts heir from French, and the silent h is restored after Latin spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语从法语借入 heir，并依照拉丁拼写补回了不发音的 h。

items.en: The feminine form heiress appears, and the word spreads to titles and traditions.
items.cn: 阴性形式 heiress 出现，这个词也扩展到头衔与传统的承袭。

note.en: Heir belongs to a legal family of inheritance words such as inherit, hereditary, and legacy, and sits close to everyday words for successors.
note.cn: heir 属于「继承」这一法律语族，与 inherit、hereditary、legacy 同族，也和日常的「后继者」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to receive money or property from someone who has died
entries.definitionCN: 继承财产；与 heir 同出拉丁语 heres 词干

entries.definition: passed from parents to children, or inherited by law
entries.definitionCN: 遗传的；世袭的；与 heir 共享拉丁语 hereditarius 词干

entries.definition: a woman who is an heir, especially to a large fortune
entries.definitionCN: 女继承人；由 heir 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成

entries.definition: a person who takes over a job or position from someone else
entries.definitionCN: 继任者；侧重接替职位，不一定是亲属

entries.definition: a person related to someone who lived a long time ago
entries.definitionCN: 后裔；侧重血缘谱系，不一定有继承权

entries.definition: the children or young of a person or animal
entries.definitionCN: 子女；后代；只强调生育关系

normalIntro.en: Heir is a legal word first: it names the person whose name is written on the will and waits for the key to be handed over.
normalIntro.cn: heir 首先是法律词：它指名字写在遗嘱上、等着钥匙交到手里的人。

normal.en: The silent h comes from Latin spelling, so the word is pronounced like air.
normal.cn: 不发音的 h 来自拉丁拼写，所以读音接近 air。

normal.en: Heir and inherit share a stem, so an heir is the person who does the inheriting.
normal.cn: heir 与 inherit 同源，heir 就是执行继承的那个人。

normal.en: The phrase heir to the throne always points to a person, never to a thing.
normal.cn: 搭配 heir to the throne 总是指向人，而不是物。

normal.en: Heiress adds a feminine ending, and heirloom is the object handed down.
normal.cn: heiress 加了阴性词尾，heirloom 则是传下来的物件。

normal.en: Compare heir with successor: an heir usually takes by family right, a successor by appointment.
normal.cn: 对比 successor：heir 多凭家族权利承袭，successor 多凭任命接替。

abstract.en: See a lawyer reading a will while a young man waits outside the door.
abstract.cn: 想象律师在宣读遗嘱，一个年轻人等在门外。

abstract.en: Picture a crown being set aside for the next person in line.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠被放到一旁，留给队伍里的下一个人。

abstract.en: Think of a story handed from one storyteller to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事从一位讲述者手中传到下一位。

examples.en: The old farmer left the land to his only heir.
examples.cn: 这位老农把土地留给了自己唯一的继承人。

examples.en: Several heirs came together to divide the family business.
examples.cn: 几位继承人聚在一起分割家族产业。

examples.en: Many young poets see themselves as heirs to the romantic age.
examples.cn: 许多年轻诗人把自己看作浪漫主义时代的传承者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哎儿」——老人临别一声叹息，家产就交给那个「哎儿」般的儿子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 heres（继承人）→ 拉丁形容词 hereditarius（遗传的、世袭的）→ 古法语 heir → 英语 heir，核心义「被留下接收遗产的人」；英语后来仿拉丁拼写补入不发音的 h。

sensesIntro.en: Heir starts as the person legally named to take property, moves to the one next in line for a throne or office, and then stretches to anyone who carries on a tradition or inherits a burden.
sensesIntro.cn: heir 先指法律上被写明接管财产的人，再指排在下一位接掌王位或职务的人，最后扩展到延续传统或「继承」负担的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name on the will waiting for the key to the house.
core.cn: 核心意象：遗嘱上的一个名字，等着老宅的钥匙交到手里。

branches.en: The everyday legal sense: the person who receives the estate.
branches.cn: 日常的法律义项：接收家产的人。

branches.en: Thrones and offices are inherited, so the sense shifts from land to position.
branches.cn: 王位与职务也像财产一样往下传，所以义项从土地转向职位。

branches.en: Traditions are treated as an inheritance, producing the cultural sense.
branches.cn: 传统被当作一份遗产，于是产生文化层面的义项。

branches.en: What is passed down may be a problem rather than a gift, producing the metaphor of inherited burdens.
branches.cn: 传下来的可能不是礼物而是问题，于是产生「继承负担」的隐喻。

branches.en: Property, titles, and traditions all pass down in the same line of succession.
branches.cn: 财产、头衔与传统的传承走的是同一条继承顺序。

intro.en: Heir is a short borrowed stem with no common suffix of its own, but English builds heiress, heirship, heirless, and heirloom around it.
intro.cn: heir 是一个短小的借词词干，本身不带常见后缀，但英语围绕它构成了 heiress、heirship、heirless 与 heirloom。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres means an heir, and its stem hered- gives hereditarius, the source of hereditary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 heres 意为继承人，其词干 hered- 构成 hereditarius，即 hereditary 的来源。

items.example: Heres names the person who takes the estate.
items.exampleCN: heres 指接收遗产的人。

items.meaning: stem of an heir, as in hereditary
items.example: The stem hered- carries the idea of inheritance.
items.exampleCN: 词干 hered- 承载「继承」的含义。

items.example: Heir keeps the legal meaning intact.
items.exampleCN: heir 完整保留了法律含义。

items.example: The suffix -ess forms heiress from heir.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ess 把 heir 构成 heiress。

items.meaningCN: 表示身份或地位的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ship forms heirship, the status of being an heir.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ship 构成 heirship，即继承人身份。

items.example: The suffix -less forms heirless, without an heir.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 heirless，意为没有继承人。

items.example: The adjective hereditary in English has no final -al, only -ary from Latin.
items.exampleCN: 英语 hereditary 末尾是来自拉丁语的 -ary，而不是 -al。

items.meaning: an object passed down through a family
items.example: The compound joins heir with an old word for a tool.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把 heir 与一个表示「器具」的旧词结合在一起。

items.meaning: to receive property from a person who died
items.example: Inherit shares the Latin stem with heir.
items.exampleCN: inherit 与 heir 共享同一拉丁词干。

definition_en: a very light, colourless gas that does not burn or react easily, used to fill balloons and in some kinds of light
core_image: 一只只气球轻轻飘向天花板，拖着细线不肯落下
scene: 生日派对结束后，几只气球一直贴着天花板，谁也没去管。After the birthday party, a few balloons filled with helium stayed pressed against the ceiling all night.
sceneCN: 这里 helium 是「氦气」（第 1 个义项：又轻又不燃的气体）；句意：生日派对结束后，几只充了氦气的气球整夜贴着天花板。

derivatives.zh: 氦四同位素，最普遍的一种氦原子
氦三同位素，常用于低温物理研究
充了氦气的，由 helium 与 filled 复合而成

senses.title: The light inert gas used in balloons
senses.definition: a colourless, odourless gas that is much lighter than air and does not burn, often used to fill party balloons and airships
senses.definitionCN: 一种无色无味、比空气轻得多且不会燃烧的气体，常用来充派对气球和飞艇
senses.example: The balloons rose quickly because they were filled with helium.
senses.exampleCN: 这些气球因为充了氦气而迅速升空。
senses.why: He was found in the sun before it was found on Earth, so the name itself means the solar element, and the gas is best known for rising.
senses.whyCN: 氦先是在太阳上被发现、后来才在地球上找到，所以名字本身意为「太阳的」元素，而这种气体最出名的特点就是往上升。

senses.title: The second lightest chemical element
senses.definition: the chemical element of atomic number two, the second most abundant element in the universe after hydrogen
senses.definitionCN: 原子序数为二的化学元素，在宇宙中的丰度仅次于氢
senses.example: Stars turn hydrogen into helium in their cores.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星在核心把氢变成氦。
senses.why: The everyday balloon gas is also a basic element, and its place on the periodic table explains the bigger scientific sense.
senses.whyCN: 日常的气球气体本身也是一种基本元素，它在元素周期表上的位置解释了更大的科学义项。

senses.title: Liquid helium as a coolant
senses.definition: helium cooled to a very low temperature and used to keep magnets, sensors, or experiments extremely cold
senses.definitionCN: 被冷却到极低温度的氦，用来让磁体、传感器或实验装置保持极低温
senses.example: The scanner needs a steady supply of liquid helium to work.
senses.exampleCN: 这台扫描仪需要持续的液氦供应才能工作。
senses.why: Helium stays a liquid at temperatures colder than any other substance allows, so it became the everyday coolant of very cold machines.
senses.whyCN: 氦比其他任何物质都能在更低的温度下保持液态，因此成了超低温设备的日常冷却剂。

senses.title: A voice made high and thin
senses.definition: the high, funny voice that a person gets after breathing in helium, because sound travels faster in it than in air
senses.definitionCN: 吸入氦气后发出的又高又怪的声音，因为声音在氦中比在空气中传播得更快
senses.example: After one breath of helium, his voice went up two octaves.
senses.exampleCN: 吸了一口氦气之后，他的嗓音高了好几个音阶。
senses.why: Because helium is so light, sound races through it, which raises the pitch in the throat and gives the word a playful everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 因为氦气极轻，声音在其中跑得更快，使喉部的音高升高，这个词也因此有了幽默的日常用法。

intro.en: Helium is a modern scientific coinage built on Greek helios, the sun, because astronomers first detected the element in sunlight.
intro.cn: helium 是现代科学造词，构自希腊语 helios（太阳），因为天文学家最早是在太阳光里发现这种元素的。

items.en: Helios is the Greek word and god of the sun.
items.cn: helios 是希腊语中「太阳」一词，也是太阳神之名。

items.en: Astronomers see a yellow line in the solar spectrum that no known element explains.
items.cn: 天文学家在太阳光谱中看到一条黄色谱线，已知元素都解释不了。

items.en: The new element is named helium, the metallic-looking form of a name taken from helios.
items.cn: 新元素被命名为 helium，即在 helios 之后加上了看似金属的拉丁词尾。

items.en: Helium is finally isolated on Earth from a gas given off by uranium minerals.
items.cn: 氦终于在地球上从铀矿物释放的气体中被分离出来。

items.en: Modern English uses helium for airships, cryogenics, and helium balloons.
items.cn: 现代英语中的 helium 用于飞艇、低温技术以及氦气球。

note.en: Helium sits in a family of science words built on Greek helios, the sun, and it is close in meaning to ordinary gas and light-air words.
note.cn: helium 属于以希腊语 helios（太阳）为词根的科技词族，在意思上与普通的气体词和「轻气体」类词相邻。

entries.definition: treating the sun as the centre of the solar system
entries.definitionCN: 以太阳为中心的；与 helium 共享希腊词根 helios

entries.definition: a purple flower that turns to follow the sun, or a gemstone of that colour
entries.definitionCN: 随太阳转向的紫色花；日光石；同出 helios 词根

entries.definition: a prefix meaning sun, as in helioscope
entries.definitionCN: 表示「太阳」的构词成分，只是外观相近，拼写几乎相同

entries.definition: a substance like air that has no fixed shape
entries.definitionCN: 气体；更宽的上位概念，氦是其中一种

entries.definition: the lightest chemical element, a colourless gas that burns easily
entries.definitionCN: 氢；宇宙中最轻、最常见的元素，常与氦并提

entries.definition: able to float or keep things floating
entries.definitionCN: 能漂浮的；与充氦气的气球直接相关

normalIntro.en: Helium keeps its Greek sun in its spelling: helios means sun, and -ium is the ending of modern element names.
normalIntro.cn: helium 在拼写上保留了希腊语的「太阳」：helios 意为太阳，-ium 则是现代元素名称的词尾。

normal.en: The stem helio- means sun in heliocentric and heliotrope, just as it does in helium.
normal.cn: 词干 helio- 在 heliocentric 与 heliotrope 中都表示太阳，helium 也一样。

normal.en: The ending -ium marks an element, like sodium or titanium, so helium is a chemical element by form.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ium 标记化学元素，如 sodium、titanium，所以从形式上看 helium 就是一种元素。

normal.en: Helium and hydrogen are neighbours on the periodic table, both very light and colourless.
normal.cn: helium 与 hydrogen 在元素周期表上相邻，都极轻且无色。

normal.en: Liquid helium is famous as the coolant of very cold machines such as medical scanners.
normal.cn: liquid helium 以其作为医学扫描仪等超低温设备的冷却剂而闻名。

normal.en: Compare the pair balloon and airship: both need helium or another gas lighter than air.
normal.cn: 对比 balloon 与 airship：两者都需要氦气或其他比空气轻的气体。

abstract.en: Watch a thin string rise and lose its straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线慢慢升起，最后不再笔直。

abstract.en: Picture the sun and a tiny piece of it caught in a glass jar.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳，以及被封进玻璃罐里的一小撮「太阳物质」。

abstract.en: Imagine a frosted pipe breathing white mist in a lab.
abstract.cn: 想象实验室里一根结霜的管子冒着白雾。

examples.en: The children let the helium balloons go and watched them climb.
examples.cn: 孩子们放开了氦气球，看着它们一路升空。

examples.en: Liquid helium keeps the superconducting magnets cool.
examples.cn: 液氦让超导磁体保持低温。

examples.en: Helium is so light that it escapes from the atmosphere.
examples.cn: 氦气太轻，会从大气层中逃逸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨脸」——气球飘到贴住天花板，高兴得「嗨」得满脸通红；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 helios（太阳）→ 科学拉丁语 helium（一八六八年依太阳光谱命名）→ 英语 helium，核心义「来自太阳的轻元素」。

sensesIntro.en: Helium begins with the everyday balloon gas, widens to the element in the periodic table, narrows again to the very cold liquid, and ends with the funny high voice it gives.
sensesIntro.cn: helium 从日常的气球气体开始，扩展到元素周期表上的元素，再收窄为超低温的液氦，最后落在吸入后变尖的嗓音上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string pulled tight to the ceiling by an unseen upward force.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股看不见的上升之力把细线拉向天花板。

branches.en: The rising balloon is the everyday sense everyone knows.
branches.cn: 上升的气球是人人都熟悉的日常义项。

branches.en: The same gas is the lightest element after hydrogen in the periodic table.
branches.cn: 同一种气体，也是元素周期表上仅次于氢的轻元素。

branches.en: Cooled far enough, helium becomes the liquid that keeps machines cold.
branches.cn: 冷却到足够低的温度，氦就成为让设备保持低温的液体。

branches.en: Because sound travels fast through it, a breath of helium raises the voice.
branches.cn: 因为声音在其中传播得快，吸一口氦气就使嗓音变高。

branches.en: The balloon, the element, and the liquid are one substance seen at different scales.
branches.cn: 气球、元素与液氦是同一种物质在不同尺度下的样子。

intro.en: Helium is built from the Greek root helio- for sun plus the modern element ending -ium, and English adds compounds such as helium-filled.
intro.cn: helium 由表示太阳的希腊词根 helio- 加上现代元素词尾 -ium 构成，英语还把它嵌进 helium-filled 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The name is scientific Latin, formed in 1868 to describe that metallic-looking substance whose light had only been seen in the sun.
latinIntro.cn: 这个名字属于科学拉丁语，一八六八年制造出来，用来指一种只在太阳光里见过、外观像金属的物质。

items.example: Helios supplies the first part of helium.
items.exampleCN: helios 提供 helium 的前半部分。

items.example: The form helio- appears in heliocentric and heliotrope.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 helio- 出现在 heliocentric 与 heliotrope 中。

items.example: The suffix -ium gives helium its element feel.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ium 让 helium 带上元素名的风格。

items.example: Helium keeps the scientific name unchanged.
items.exampleCN: helium 保留了原来的科学名称。

items.meaningCN: 表示水的词根，见于 hydrogen
items.example: Hydro- makes hydrogen, helium is neighbour and a frequent contrast.
items.exampleCN: hydro- 构成 hydrogen，它与 helium 相邻，常被拿来对比。

items.example: The compound helium-filled describes party balloons.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 helium-filled 用来描述派对气球。

items.example: The form -like appears in helium-like, meaning resembling helium.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 helium-like，意为类似氦的。

items.meaning: a substance that fills any space
items.example: The noun gas is the simple class word for helium.
items.exampleCN: gas 是 helium 所属的简单类别词。

items.meaning: the mixture of gases we breathe
items.example: The word air helps define helium by contrast, being heavier.
items.exampleCN: air 可用来反衬 helium，因为空气更重。

definition_en: a curve that winds evenly around a central line, like the shape of a spring or the spiral on a snail shell
core_image: 一根弹簧被人轻轻拉开，一圈一圈绕着看不见的中轴往上走
scene: 生物课上，老师让学生沿着一支螺旋形的楼梯向上看。In the biology class, the teacher asked the students to look up along the staircase built as a helix.
sceneCN: 这里 helix 是「螺旋形」（第 1 个义项：绕着中轴盘旋上升的曲线）；句意：生物课上，老师让学生沿这座螺旋形楼梯向上看。

derivatives.zh: 螺旋形的，由 helix 加形容词后缀 -al 构成
螺旋状的，由 helic- 词干加希腊语词尾 -oid 构成
呈螺旋状的，由 helix 与 shaped 复合而成

senses.title: A winding curve around a central axis
senses.definition: a continuous curve that turns around a straight central line while moving forward, like the thread of a screw or a spring
senses.definitionCN: 一边绕着一根笔直的中轴一边向前的连续曲线，像螺丝纹路或弹簧的形状
senses.example: The wire is bent into a tight helix.
senses.exampleCN: 这根金属丝被弯成一个紧实的螺旋。
senses.why: The Greek helissein means to turn round, so the word at first simply names a curly shape as a thing that keeps turning.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 helissein 意为「旋转」，这个词最初就是把「不停转圈」这一形状直接命名为一样东西。

senses.title: The curved rim of the outer ear
senses.definition: the raised curved edge of the outer ear, which folds inward like the rim of a shell
senses.definitionCN: 外耳边缘隆起的弧状部分，像贝壳的边一样向内卷
senses.example: The ear helix was slightly bruised after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔倒之后，他的耳轮有点擦伤。
senses.why: Ancient anatomy borrowed the word for any rolled rim, and the curled edge of the ear looks just like a small spiral.
senses.whyCN: 古代解剖学用这个词指各种向内卷的边，而耳朵卷曲的边缘看起来就像一个小螺旋。

senses.title: The coiled double strand of DNA
senses.definition: one of the two twisted strands in the ladder-like structure of a DNA molecule, which winds in a double helix
senses.definitionCN: 脱氧核糖核酸分子梯状结构中两条相互缠绕的链之一，整体呈双螺旋
senses.example: Each helix of the molecule carries a sequence of bases.
senses.exampleCN: 分子中的每条螺旋都带着一串碱基序列。
senses.why: Modern science needed a ready name for the twisted ladder of DNA, and the old word for a winding curve fitted exactly.
senses.whyCN: 现代科学需要现成的词来形容脱氧核糖核酸那道扭曲的梯子，而古已有之的「盘旋曲线」一词恰好吻合。

senses.title: A curled shell, such as a snail shell
senses.definition: the spiral shell of a snail or of a related sea creature
senses.definitionCN: 蜗牛或类似海生动物的螺旋状外壳
senses.example: The garden snail carries a pale helix on its back.
senses.exampleCN: 花园里的蜗牛背上驮着一只浅色的螺旋壳。
senses.why: The same turning line that draws a curve also describes the growth of a shell, so the word names the whole shape as well as its line.
senses.whyCN: 画出曲线的同一条旋转线也描述了贝壳的生长方式，所以这个词既指那道线，也指整个形状。

intro.en: Helix comes from Greek helix, a spiral or a twist, built on the verb helissein, to turn round; English took it first through Latin.
intro.cn: helix 源自希腊语 helix（螺旋、卷曲），源于动词 helissein（旋转）；英语是经由拉丁语先把它吸收进来的。

items.en: Helissein means to turn round or to roll, and the noun helix names anything twisted.
items.cn: helissein 意为旋转、卷动，名词 helix 指任何卷曲之物。

items.en: Latin keeps helix for a spiral thing and the helix of the ear.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 helix，用来指螺旋物以及耳朵的耳轮。

items.en: Mathematicians adopt helix as the name of a curve that winds at a steady angle.
items.cn: 数学家在十六世纪采用 helix 来称呼以固定角度盘绕的曲线。

items.en: English use spreads from botany and anatomy to geometry and mechanics.
items.cn: 英语中的用法从植物学与解剖学扩展到几何学与力学。

items.en: The double helix of DNA makes the word famous worldwide.
items.cn: 脱氧核糖核酸的双螺旋使这个词在全世界扬名。

note.en: Helix is the Latin and Greek relative of the helio- family only in spelling, and it sits beside everyday words for winding forms.
note.cn: helix 与 helio- 词族只是拼写相近，词源不同；在意思上，它与描写盘绕形状的日常词相邻。

entries.definition: the Latin-style plural of helix
entries.definitionCN: helix 的拉丁式复数，意思是多个螺旋

entries.definition: arranged in the form of a helix
entries.definitionCN: 螺旋形的；由 helix 加 -al 构成的形容词

entries.definition: a combining form meaning sun, as in helium
entries.definitionCN: 表示太阳的构词成分，如 helium；只是拼写相近，词源不同的希腊词

entries.definition: a curve that winds around and around from a fixed point
entries.definitionCN: 螺旋；侧重从中心向外盘旋，与 helix 常用作近义词

entries.definition: a length of wire or rope wound into loops
entries.definitionCN: 盘绕的一圈；线圈；强调缠绕而成的实物

entries.definition: a bend or turn in something along its length
entries.definitionCN: 扭；弯曲；指形状沿长度方向扭曲

normalIntro.en: Helix names a line that keeps turning while it moves forward, so almost everything wound and rising shares its shape.
normalIntro.cn: helix 指一条边转圈边向前的线，几乎所有卷起来又向上升的东西都带着它的形状。

normal.en: The Greek verb helissein means to turn round, and helix is the noun built on it.
normal.cn: 希腊语动词 helissein 意为旋转，helix 就是在它之上造出的名词。

normal.en: Helix has two plurals: helixes from English habit and helices from Latin.
normal.cn: helix 有两个复数：英语习惯的 helixes 与拉丁式的 helices。

normal.en: The adjective helical appears in helical gears, whose teeth run at an angle.
normal.cn: 形容词 helical 常见于 helical gears（斜齿轮），其齿是斜着排的。

normal.en: The double helix is the familiar twisted ladder of DNA.
normal.cn: double helix 就是我们在生物书里熟悉的脱氧核糖核酸扭曲梯状结构。

normal.en: Compare spiral and helix: a spiral widens as it turns, a helix keeps the same width.
normal.cn: 对比 spiral 与 helix：spiral 盘旋时越转越大，helix 的宽度保持不变。

abstract.en: Hold a phone cord and let it fall into its old coiled loops.
abstract.cn: 握住一根电话线，让它垂下来，恢复成一圈圈卷曲。

abstract.en: Draw a line around a pole with a pencil, going slowly up.
abstract.cn: 用铅笔绕着一根杆画线，慢慢往上走。

abstract.en: Watch a vine climb round a thin branch.
abstract.cn: 想象一根藤蔓绕着细枝向上攀爬。

examples.en: The spring is formed into a helix that stretches easily.
examples.cn: 这根弹簧被做成易于拉伸的螺旋形。

examples.en: Scientists described the double helix in the middle of the last century.
examples.cn: 科学家在上世纪中叶描述了双螺旋结构。

examples.en: A thin helix of smoke rose from the candle.
examples.cn: 一缕细细的烟从蜡烛上升起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑利克斯」——黑夜里利索地盘旋而上的螺旋楼梯；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 helissein（旋转）→ 希腊语 helix（螺旋、卷曲之物）→ 拉丁语 helix → 英语 helix，核心义「绕着中轴螺旋上升的形状」。

sensesIntro.en: Helix begins with the geometric curve, takes a body part in anatomy, becomes the famous double strand of DNA, and finally names a curled shell.
sensesIntro.cn: helix 从几何曲线开始，在解剖学里指身体部位，又成为闻名世界的脱氧核糖核酸双螺旋，最后也指盘旋的贝壳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the thread of a screw climbing around an invisible axis.
core.cn: 核心意象：螺丝的纹路绕着一根看不见的中轴向上攀升。

branches.en: The geometry sense is the plain ordinary meaning of the word.
branches.cn: 几何义项是这个词最本色的日常含义。

branches.en: The curled rim of the ear is the anatomical sense.
branches.cn: 卷曲的耳轮是解剖学义项。

branches.en: The twisted ladder of DNA is the scientific double strand sense.
branches.cn: 扭曲的脱氧核糖核酸梯子是科学上的双螺旋义项。

branches.en: A coiled snail shell shows the same curve in a solid form.
branches.cn: 蜗牛的螺旋壳把同样的曲线呈现在一个实体上。

branches.en: Ear rims and shells both show the same rolled edge that mathematics describes.
branches.cn: 耳轮与贝壳都呈现出数学所描述的那种卷边形状。

intro.en: Helix is a Greek stem that English mostly keeps whole, adding adjectives such as helical and compounds such as helix-shaped.
intro.cn: helix 是一个希腊词干，英语多数情况下原样保留，只加上 helical 这类形容词与 helix-shaped 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin took over Greek helix unchanged and handed it on to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语原样吸纳了希腊语 helix，再传给英语。

items.example: Helissein supplies the idea of turning.
items.exampleCN: helissein 提供「转动」这层意思。

items.example: Helix is the direct Greek source.
items.exampleCN: helix 是直接来源。

items.example: Helix keeps the shape named in Greek.
items.exampleCN: helix 保留了希腊语所命名的形状。

items.example: The stem helic- appears in helicopter, a spinning wing.
items.exampleCN: 词干 helic- 见于 helicopter，意为旋转的翼。

items.example: The suffix -al forms helical.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 helical。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms helicoid, spiral-like.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oid 构成 helicoid，意为螺旋状的。

items.meaningCN: 借词中表示复数的词尾
items.example: The ending -es turns helix into helices.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -es 把 helix 变成 helices。

items.example: The adjective double forms the common phrase double helix.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 double 构成常见搭配 double helix。

items.example: The suffix -shaped forms helix-shaped.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -shaped 构成 helix-shaped。

latinEntries.meaning: a spiral, the rim of the ear
